That is until this weekend, when computer historians made the game accessible on modern hardware.

Another game has remained buried.

Earlier, he told TMZ that the best part of attending Miley’s wedding was “knowing that the love is going to last forever.”.

In a recent development, us previously reported that Miley was walked down the aisle by her mother, Tish Cyrus, who attended the nuptials with her husband, Dominic Purcell. (Miley’s sisters, Noah Cyrus and Brandi Cyrus, were both in attendance, as was Liz’s son Damian Hurley.).

“It was a really intimate wedding, and there weren’t any big celebrity guests outside of her family,” a source exclusively told Us, adding, “It wasn’t a typical Hollywood or traditional wedding, but was everything Miley wanted.”.

She subsequently thanked her team for pulling off the glamorous ceremony while acknowledging that her wedding coincided with another major milestone.

Latest Update: Unofficial GTA 6 PC port effort suffers setback as Rockstar seemingly takes down Project Leonida, one of the internet's biggest recompilation projects

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A lot has happened in the last 24 hours in the community working to get Grand Theft Auto 6 running on PC.
  • Industry observers note that after infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6, the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers.
  • In a recent development, the largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A lot has happened in the last 24 hours in the community working to get Grand Theft Auto 6 running on PC. And now, Rockstar has dealt a major blow to their efforts.

Industry observers note that after infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6, the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers. Their goal? Get the game playable on PC as soon as possible.

In a recent development, the largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC. Rockstar has allegedly taken down the server, causing the project's leaders to dismantle the entire operation.

Project Leonida's lead NotRexed posted on X to announce they're ending development, after fans noticed the Discord server has been removed, as has Project Leonida's GitHub repository.

According to recent reports, "I quit guys. I'm sorry," NotRexed wrote. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can't control so I'm stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.".

The modder, who claims to be a "15 year-old kid", later wrote in a follow-up X post that Rockstar is behind the server's takedown, though that's not the only reason for the project's end.

"Last post from me. I wanna clear things up," they wrote. "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've said before, I'm a 15 year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.".

Sources indicate that before the Project Leonida server disappeared, footage emerged showing GTA 6 running on PC. The game is able to reach the initial setup screen, but promptly goes into a black screen afterwards. As unimpressive as the result was, it was achieved within hours of the full Xbox build's leak.

Incidentally, while Project Leonida was the biggest and most prominent of the various GTA 6 recompilation projects, the leaking of the full Xbox build has given rise to various other groups. PortWatch VI is a website dedicated to tracking their progress, and though the data is almost entirely self-reported, a few other teams appear to have made notable progress themselves, so this may not be the end of the story.

Rockstar has yet to comment publicly on the Xbox build's leak, and the company has not revealed GTA 6 for PC. However, a report suggested GTA 6 arrives on PC in the first quarter of 2027, earlier than everyone expected.

If you're among the millions already playing the game on consoles, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough contains a wealth of information covering all major mechanics, main missions, secrets, cheats and more besides.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's been an exciting addition to the Nintendo Classics GameCube app today, as users have discovered a small - but oft-requested - change in the software's Version 2.2.0.
  • In a recent development, this new option arrived fairly quietly as part of an enhancement that otherwise introduced Wave Race: Blue Storm to the Nintendo Classics – GameCube lineup.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been an exciting addition to the Nintendo Classics GameCube app today, as users have discovered a small - but oft-requested - change in the software's Version 2.2.0.

In a recent development, this new option arrived fairly quietly as part of an enhancement that otherwise introduced Wave Race: Blue Storm to the Nintendo Classics – GameCube lineup. That addition may have generated the most headlines, but it's this one little toggle that's getting many players exicted.

Why is this such a massive deal? Previously, the bordered image on the 4:3 aspect ratio games contained lots of little dots, and players complained that these were distracting at best, and casused discomfort on the eyes whilst playing at worst. Other players worried it would contribute to screen burn-in on older televsion sets. As part of the new patch, you can simply border your games with plain black - a tiny revision, but one that you can already see online communities celebrating. The player icon (another UI element that attracts derision) is still present, however, but as one comment summarises: "it's a step in the right direction".

"Oh my gawd, I've been wanting this! I hate the checkered on the side, it clashed with every game I tried," states one social media user." Players have been complaining about these borders and UI elements since Nintendo Classics was introduced on the Nintendo Switch back on 18th September, 2018. So it's taken a good eight years for Nintendo to - finally - implement a change.

Recent findings suggest that in order to change the border yourself, you need to head to the game library selection screen on the Nintendo Classics app, navigate to the game settings, and locate the option to toggle this border graphic in the "Extra Elements Display" tab. Hit the button and - bang - you're done. At the time of writing, this option only appears on the GameCue app, and only on Switch 2, but people on social media are already asking Nintendo to enable it across the original Switch and other apps in the library, too.

Not everyone is happy with the 'slowly, slowly' approach Nintendo is taking towards implementing these changes, though. "Why can't we expect the full step with no graphic at all?" asks one irritated poster on Reddit. "Why do you have to deal with these half assed implementations for a paid deluxe subscription service?".

"Oh well, probably gotta wait another 10 years for the next improvement" states another. Another slightly more constructive user outlines what helpful additons might look like, noting that adding a "blurred zoomed in image of the game to fill out the background, or just extending the colors outward into the border, or maybe something fun like a CRT TV-looking border like the NES and SNES Classic had" would go a long way to make the retro experience better on the consoles.

Fans who spent years watching the Marvel movies in order are gearing up for the shared universe's next big crossover event with Avengers: Doomsday. Arguably the most anticipated upcoming Marvel movie in years, the blockbuster has been steadily building excitement since those teasers arrived back in January. Now Joe Russo explained why they decided to give us footage that early.

We recently got the final Doomsday trailer, which instantly went viral thanks to epic moments from Cyclops and Steve Rogers. What we know about Avengers: Doomsday is still limited, but the excitement building around the movie has been steadily building for months. While at Qatar Film Committee’s second Doha Industry Days (via Deadline) Russo spoke about this unique marketing strategy, offering:.

Sources indicate that I have to work extra hard to subvert your expectations and be aware of who you are as a viewer and how you’re changing. The last time I did this, in 2018, 2019, is very different than now because we’ve been through a pandemic; lots of people spent a lot of time on social media. Movies saw a tremendous downturn, streaming saw a tremendous upturn, and now that all seems to be reversing. So, it shifts constantly. You have to be a futurist to try to predict where the market is going.

Marvel is known for its tight security, so it was surprising that we got footage from Doomsday so many months before the movie's December release. The industry has changed a bit since Endgame arrived in theaters, and the MCU has had a number of box office blunders including bombs like The Marvels. As such, The Russos wanted get the hype train running early, with more news, casting, and footage methodically released to the public.

Later in the same appearance, Russo went on to share how audiences have changed over the years. As such Endgame followed the chairs casting announcement with four exciting teasers. As he put it:.

I have to interact with the fans in order to understand what is moving them, what is working for them. What we’ve been doing with Doomsday is very different than the last time we did this because the speed of conversation on the internet is even faster than it was in 2018, 2019. I had this idea, why don’t we start the story a year early? Why don’t we start dropping clues in the year leading up to the movie… we did four trailers that were sprinkled out.

It has been revealed that those brief clips quickly went viral, especially the Captain America teaser that confirmed Chris Evans was returning as Steve Rogers. With the next Avengers movie now just a few weeks away from its release, anticipation has reached a fever pitch that should (hopefully) result in massive box office numbers. Perhaps future MCU projects will follow this same strategy.

Industry observers note that we'll find out shortly as Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list. Marvel might be in for a one-two punch, as Spider-Man: Brand Newly introduced Day broke Endgame's box office record just a few months ago.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when my partner and I were starting a family, we searched high and low for a place outside Upcoming York where we could imagine our future children growing up.
  • In a recent development, it looked like something out of a medieval fairy tale.
  • Our twins’ arrival was imminent, so we made an offer in February, closed in April, and brought home babies Grace and Noah on Memorial Day weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when my partner and I were starting a family, we searched high and low for a place outside Upcoming York where we could imagine our future children growing up. We looked upstate, in Connecticut, and at all those charming hamlets strung along the eastern end of Long Island known as the Hamptons. Toured hundreds of houses, clicked thousands of listings. But not one felt like home.

Nevins in her garden in East Hampton.

In a recent development, it looked like something out of a medieval fairy tale. A great furrowed trunk rising from a froth of flowering vines that split into enormous limbs sweeping improbably far across the garden. Its arrangement was so baroque—veiny, muscular wood twisting and reaching, dissolving overhead into a canopy of green delicacy. We could picture our children climbing its winding branches, little hands against its ridged, mossy bark.

Our twins’ arrival was imminent, so we made an offer in February, closed in April, and brought home babies Grace and Noah on Memorial Day weekend. Now we joke that we didn’t buy a house—we bought this tree.

Recent findings suggest that but what is it? A butternut tree? An oak? A black walnut? Deborah Nevins, one of the most revered living landscape designers, created this garden for the previous owners in 2004. In the fall, she invited me to her white-shingled cottage in Springs, East Hampton, to find out. Her living room has triple-hung windows like those in Monticello, Thomas Jefferson’s house in Virginia, which go down to the floor so it’s easy to wheel in her potted lemon trees when the seasons change. “Winter is divine; it’s when they bloom,” she coos. “The house smells of lemon blossoms.”.

David Geffen’s pool at his former Beverly Hills estate, once home to Warner Bros.’ Jack Warner.

Recent findings suggest that “Butternut!” she declares, slamming the book shut with all the force of her petite five-foot-nothing frame. “For sure.”.

This is our tree. A butternut that likely sprouted generations before she came along. “It’s a native tree, probably a hundred years old. But I’d have to know the caliper—the diameter about a foot up—to be more precise.” She decided it’d be the anchor for our yard design the moment she saw it—existing mature trees are “sacred” and must be preserved at all costs. At its base, she dared to plant clematis, usually a climbing vine, that now rambles across the ground, softening the old tree’s trunk with a tangle of flowers. The butternut divides the rest of the property into distinct passages, including an ornamental reflecting pool bordered by hornbeam hedges, a lap pool shaded under locust trees, and a gravel path lined with rounded boxwoods.

Sources indicate that GREEK MYTHOLOGY It took Nevins eight years and some 20 trips to Greece to complete her collaboration with architect Renzo Piano on the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center. What was once a parking lot is now planted with more than 1,500 trees, 128,000 shrubs and perennials, and 164,000 grass plugs.

A rendering of the 40-acre park at the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center in Athens.

To Nevins, the tree is an excellent example of her greater gardening philosophy: “I’m interested in creating unfolding spaces which intensify [the viewers’] experience, your sense of place and movement through a garden,” she says. She frequently builds hedges and allées to control viewers’ attention, like horse blinders. “Not every aspect of the garden is seen at once. You have to stop and think.”.

Over the last four decades, Nevins has been entrusted with the grounds of some extraordinary spaces. Her clients include media mogul David Geffen, fashion designer Tommy Hilfiger, former Disney chairman Michael Eisner, and hotelier Ian Schrager. Commissions can range from tiny residential spaces (like mine) to huge commercial projects abroad. It took her eight years and some 20 trips to Greece to complete a 40-acre park at the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center in Athens. That was a collaboration with architect Renzo Piano on a landscape that climbs over the buildings themselves, planted with native grasses from the hills of Attica and fragrant Mediterranean herbs, including lavender, rosemary, and oregano. Nevins’s mantra for the project was simple: “Speak Greek.” The execution was anything but simple. More than 1,500 trees, 128,000 shrubs and perennials, and 164,000 grass plugs fill the public work. Nevins conceptualized the totality of the park. “I chose every single tree!” she claims. “We had to propagate hundreds of thousands of plants throughout Greece, and we decided to hire various nurseries so that if there was a disease or fire, the entire crop would not be wiped out.” Her effort impressed Piano. “It is always special when, beyond the work on a project itself, you realize that you share the same values and ideas,” says Piano of Nevins, whom he describes as a “wonderful professional and human adventure.”.

According to recent reports, “There is discipline in her work but never rigidity,” says Scott Mitchell, the West Coast–based architect who met Nevins at a dinner honoring architect Richard Meier in 1997 and went on to work with her on properties for Geffen in both California and Fresh York. “Her landscapes don’t compete with architecture; they give it a place to belong.”.

He recalls the “emotional power” of her work for Geffen at the Warner estate in Beverly Hills, former home of Warner Bros. cofounder Jack Warner. “Endless sweeps of white azaleas, a driveway lined with ancient, gnarled native sycamores, and 11 acres of rolling meadow beneath giant coast live oaks,” Mitchell notes. “World-class projects require cohesion between architecture and landscape. They have to play from the same sheet of music. Debby totally gets that. Her response to architecture is clear and harmonious—confident but never overstepping.”.

Tommy Hilfiger and Dee Ocleppo at their Mustique estate.

Gil Schafer, a New York–based architect who has worked with Nevins on more than 25 houses and gardens, also commends her command of structure. At his own house near Millbrook, she built a 12-foot-high hornbeam enclosure nestled into the surrounding farm fields that has, he claims, “an almost abstract sculptural quality—as if Richard Serra had suddenly decided to work in hornbeam rather than Corten steel.”.

Recent findings suggest that nevins was born in Manhattan at what was then the Doctors Hospital on the Upper East Side. The family resided in the penthouse of the same building where Greta Garbo lived. Her father died of a brain tumor at 43, when Nevins was six months old, and so her mother had to return to work. At six, she was sent to Camp Taconic in Massachusetts. “I was tiny! My mother might have been arrested today.” She remembers walking in the woods, finding a strawberry, and reporting the discovery in a letter home. The seed had been planted—pun quite obvious.

Recent findings suggest that fleur Cowles, the formidable editor behind the short-lived, extravagantly inventive magazine Flair, was a maternal relative and had an outsize impact on her childhood. “She knew everyone, and she was so brilliant,” Nevins says, offering me an problem of Flair from another bookshelf like a cherished family heirloom. Another influence was her mother’s sister, Miriam Sampson, an interior decorator who lived across from Carnegie Hall. “In this big apartment, she had her office in one room, and she had little models of apartments. I was so intrigued,” Nevins recalls. She’d cut out pictures of interiors and gardens from magazines and assemble them in scrapbooks. “But I didn’t even know about this idea of being a landscape architect.”.

Sources indicate that when Nevins was 14, her mother remarried and the family moved to Fresh Haven, Connecticut. She went on to attend Boston University for undergrad and returned to New York for graduate school at Columbia. “They didn’t think that landscape history, which is what I wanted to study, was academic enough. And they probably had no one to teach it anyway,” she says. So she earned an MA and an MPhil in art history. Travel became a form of individualized study. “I learned by looking,” she says. She sought out Le Corbusier’s buildings in France, including La Tourette, Maisons Jaoul, and Villa Savoye, and drove from Paris to Santiago de Compostela looking at Romanesque and Merovingian churches. She made her first of many pilgrimages to Sissinghurst, a garden in Kent created by the writer Vita Sackville-West and her diplomat husband, Harold Nicolson. “There’s nothing more beautiful than Sissinghurst,” she sighs.

Recent findings suggest that one of Nevins’s greatest champions has been Geffen, whom Victoria Newhouse, the renowned architecture critic and widow of longtime Condé Nast chairman Si Newhouse, introduced her to. On her first meeting with Geffen, Nevins arrived to present her work with a carousel of 80 slides. “After maybe 30 slides, he claims, ‘That’s enough. You’re hired.’ And I thought to myself, Who is this guy?” When she looked him up, she read that one of his attributes is spotting talent. “And that was that.”.

In a recent development, at the Warner estate in Beverly Hills, she removed one swimming pool to open up the landscape, built a new one with a new patio house where Warner had a putting green, and relocated several mature oak trees on the property. “David is not afraid of substantial moves,” she claims. (They preserved the fountains and terraces Warner had commissioned from Florence Yoch, who designed the grounds of Tara for Gone With the Wind, of course.) However, according to Nevins, when Warner’s daughter came to see what Geffen had done, she looked around and asked if they had changed anything. “ ‘What did we change? We changed everything!’ ” Nevins remembers Geffen saying. “The idea that we didn’t do a thing is crazy, but that it looked like it was meant to be—that’s a good thing. The ultimate compliment that looks like I did nothing.”.

An aerial view of Deborah Nevins’s Hamptons garden.

In a recent development, hilfiger hired Nevins for a property in Mustique in the early 1990s, and again for his Denbigh Farm in Greenwich in 1995. In the Caribbean, she created palm promenades and a courtyard of white flowers; in Connecticut, she brought the elements of an old estate into a coherent whole. “I knew she was incredibly passionate about her work, and that always interested me because I love working with people who are passionate about what they do,” Hilfiger states. “Her execution was impeccable, and she delivered exactly what she promised.”.

Industry observers note that nevins’s office is based in Upcoming York City, and she keeps between 5 and 10 new projects going at all times. “Almost any job is interesting unless I hear in advance that the people aren’t nice,” she notes. “Also, art collectors, in my experience, have been great patrons. If you’re an art collector—and you’re truly not collecting just to make money from art—you have an interest in beauty and understanding.”.

PLEACHY KEEN “She is very intuitive, so she needs to walk a site and feel what it has to say,” architect Gil Schafer claims of Nevins. “She feels this deep kinship with the natural world, with plants and with the trees of a site, which guides how she approaches her interventions on a property.”.

According to recent reports, on average, it takes two years to get a garden up and running, three years if she needs to build fresh structures. But a garden is never finished. Roberta Denning, who with her husband, Steve, commissioned Nevins for her family’s property in Greenwich in 2006, describes the pleasure of living with something that acquires depth while continuing to change. “What she created has grown more valuable with time,” Denning indicates of her property, which includes a walking labyrinth among chestnuts and beech trees. “Nearly 20 years on, the gardens feel both that they have always been here and that they are continually renewed.” Nevins says clients have joked that hiring her is like a marriage because it’s a long-term relationship, and it requires work. “So I guess I’m a polygamist?” she smiles.

Recent findings suggest that patience is a big part of her process. “She is very intuitive, so she needs to walk a site and feel what it has to say, and this is one way that we are so similar in our approach,” Schafer notes. “You need to give her the space to read the land and sort out how she wants to approach it. I think she also feels this deep kinship with the natural world, with plants and with the trees of a site, which guides how she approaches her interventions on a property.”.

People joke that Nevins speaks to the plants, but Schafer isn’t sure it’s an act. “I think she really does!”.

“I do love them,” Nevins indicates of her botanical family. “I was at a nursery with someone the other day, and I noted, ‘It’s problematic. I get crushes on plants, but sometimes they don’t really have a place, and it’s so disappointing. It’s like a failed romance.’”.

A walking labyrinth in Greenwich, Connecticut.

Right now her crush is Stewartia pseudocamellia. “It has amazing bark, and the flower looks like a camellia, but it’s not a camellia, it’s a tree.” One plant she doesn’t love? Flowering forsythia, which Schafer reports she often refers to as “spring vomit.”.

Nevins believes her greatest asset is the ability to blend both architectural history and botanical skill. “I have such a strong academic background in architectural history,” she notes. “I know exactly what these references are that they make to historical, even modern historical buildings.”.

In another part of Long Island, Nevins combined the elements into what she calls a “beech house”—pun absolutely intentional. Martin Filler, an architecture critic and longtime contributor to The Fresh York Review of Books, met Nevins when they were graduate students in Columbia’s art history department in the early 1970s. At the time, his wife, Rosemarie Haag Bletter, an architectural historian and professor emerita of art history at the CUNY Graduate Center in New York City, was working on her PhD and teaching undergraduates. According to Filler, Nevins promised back then to design them a garden one day. “Since we didn’t have a house and never expected to, we remarked to ourselves, ‘Yeah, right,’ ” he says. “But who knew that someday we would, and that gardening would become such a large part of our lives, especially Rosemarie’s?”.

According to recent reports, in the mid-1990s, they bought a cottage that had been part of Stanford White’s Breese estate, The Orchard, in Southampton. “Debby mentioned that she would now make good on her promise to design a garden for us,” Filler remembers. “By that time she had become one of the top landscape designers, but she insisted on doing it and refused to be paid.” She stayed with them for a winter weekend and spent hours walking the property. “Then she sat down at our dining table with a roll of yellow tracing paper and the surveyor’s map, and she designed the whole thing within a few hours. She joked, ‘Don’t tell anyone how fast I was.’ ”.

It has been revealed that THE GIVING TREE When Derek C. Blasberg first saw the majestic tree in the backyard of a property in the Hamptons, he knew he’d found a home for his family. The hunt to identify it led him to Nevins’s larger body of work. “We could picture our children climbing its winding branches.”.

Recent findings suggest that the Beech House, a 16-foot-by-16-foot-by-16-foot living gazebo made of 26 purple beech trees (Fagus sylvatica “Dawyck Purple”), is the centerpiece. The trees were sourced from Buffalo, trucked to Southampton, and replanted in the same orientation in which they had been grown. (“Each tree had to be marked with a dot of blue paint to indicate due north and then planted in that same geographical direction,” Filler remembers.) They were wired and trained over a wooden inner framework shaped like the schematic outline of a house and then clipped into shape on the exterior. The floor was paved with bluestone squares and rectangles in a random-looking pattern Nevins designed.

According to recent reports, “Each year when we meet with our accountant to do our tax return, he’s always shocked that we spend so much on the garden,” Filler says. “We tell him: ‘You have clients who have boats, you have clients who have classic cars—well, this is our pleasure, our indulgence.’”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever is in the grip of a gold-farming bonanza, as Blizzard's attempts to curb them are met with a seemingly endless wave of alternative money-making methods.

It has been revealed that first, some context. Last week an exploitative method of making gold in the game was removed. The exploit involved repeatedly running the new Blackmaw Hold dungeon and swiftly killing non-elite enemies which were - mistakenly - given better loot drops than they were supposed to have. This was taken out, and people exploiting this to extreme degrees were temporarily suspended and had trading blocks put on their accounts. In addition, gold gained this way was removed from their accounts.

This was a substantial deal. For one, it was the first time Blizzard has put a stop to a specific money-making strategy in Forever. But in the days following Blizzard's action, other exploits have been discovered requiring similar action.

Industry observers note that let's start with dungeon farming. In World of Warcraft, you are limited to entering 10 separate dungeon instances per hour before the game starts locking you out. This farming method is based around rapidly entering these dungeons, killing the mobs for loot, leaving and resetting the dungeon, then rinsing and repeating. Do this 10 times and you've got a handsome payday.

It has been revealed that some players were running into the side entrance of the Uldaman dungeon to kill a specific boss, The Obsidian Sentinel, in a way that would take just a few minutes. So people were able to farm valuable boss loot and max the dungeon limit of 20-30 gold earned in an hour. This exploit has been killed, with Blizzard removing the loot from this boss to temporarily curb the strategy.

Industry observers note that this isn't without its concerns. Primarily, by removing the loot from that aforementioned Uldaman boss, several strong items have been removed for regular players. This includes one part of the beloved Pendulum of Doom axe, which is now unobtainable in-game until the loot is turned back on for the boss.

In a recent development, however, this is far from the only dungeon farming method. Players are now repeatedly farming non-boss enemies in the new Krol'dok Stronghold to earn potentially upwards of 100 gold an hour. And presumably more people are looking for more exploits all the time. Blizzard, in turn, has had to halve the instance cap in World of Warcraft: Forever to five to attempt to get control of the situation.

So that's the end of it, right? Well, no! While these instanced farms have proven lucrative, they are far from the only way of gathering vast amounts of gold. Already, players have discovered that by grouping and killing Furbolgs in Felwood, they can all pick up beads - seemingly another bug in the game. These can be exchanged for items, which in turn can be sold off to a vendor for a tidy profit.

Even if this gets patched, there are other 'valid' farms capable of turning a quick profit. You can, for example, kill turtles in Mount Hyjal and skin them for valuable leather and turtle scales, not to mention their meat and occasional trash to sell to vendors. Why is this valid while dungeon farms aren't? It raises the question: what makes a gold-farming method worth fixing?

Sources indicate that it's a tricky problem. To defend gold farmers for a moment, the game has a history of gold farming that has been permitted. For years, mages have been blasting down dungeon mobs without fear of ban nor suspension. In response to the Blackmaw Hold fix, Blizzard stated: "Finding efficient farming spots has always been a part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.".

So the line appears to be the level of profit made from a particular farm. Though without this line being drawn explicitly, one wonders how gold farmers will know whether their strategy is safe or not. There is a culture around goldfarming that has existed since the game first released in the early 2000s. These aren't bad players. They aren't even naughty players, really. They've been a part of the game's culture for over 20 years.

Industry observers note that at the same time, it's hard not to feel for the developers here. This is not the same World of Warcraft as the one players jumped into decades ago. Long gone are the days when a few guildies could accrue wealth with a humble farming method. Gold farmers are now equipped with the skills to efficiently harvest mobs with ease, and can promptly hop between server layers to access mobs quicker, and when a lucrative farm is found, it can be kept secret within Discord servers and run endlessly until Blizzard wisens up.

Industry observers note that at the same time, the developers have to stay on top of this stuff. Already the in-game economy is getting more expensive as time goes on, and those who have taken their time to level with friends are facing fiscal pressures that those who rushed through it did not encounter. All the while, Blizzard has acknowledged that gold farming is a part of the game, and so the pressure not to cater to some good ol' fashioned hustling is doubtless weighing on their shoulders.

Recent findings suggest that what will likely happen is this. Gold farmers will bounce around with the developers hot on their tails until finally the farms deemed unintended or exploitative are made untenable. That's when and where the line will be drawn. This will likely be a continuous problem as updates bring more potential money-making opportunities to the game, but it's safe to say there's an element of uncertainty surrounding the situation.

It has been revealed that the big question is whether the events of the Blackmaw Hold suspensions put enough fear into the hearts of gold farmers to curb their exploitative habits? If it hasn't, do the developers have the nerve to dish out more severe punishments? Time, as always, will be the test of it.

Sources indicate that for those of you who aren't already max level and farming gold, or trapped up in Winterspring, grinding out Wintersaber Trainers reputation for no reason (me), it's worth emphasising that World of Warcraft: Forever does bring a lot of the magic of the original game back alongside quality of life changes. Give it a go, if you dare.

Every Version of 'A Christmas Carol,' Ranked (and Where to Stream Them)

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2043 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol is the greatest story about Christmas ever written—even better than the one with Mary and Joseph and the manger.
  • I've carefully considered every major theatrical and TV adaptation of A Christmas Carol and rated each in terms of holiday spirit, Dickensian whimsy, and Scrooge-osity to arrive at the definite, no-argument-possible best-to-worst list of Christmas Carols.
  • According to recent reports, to rank Christmas Carols, you have to decide what A Christmas Carol is to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol is the greatest story about Christmas ever written—even better than the one with Mary and Joseph and the manger. The 1843 tale of a miser browbeaten by self-righteous ghosts is (probably) the most filmed story of all time. Dozens of cinematic adaptations of A Christmas Carol have been released in theaters and on TV since Scrooge; or Marley's Ghost came out in 1901. Hundreds or thousands if you count re-imaginings and very special episodes of sitcoms. But which version is the very best?

I've carefully considered every major theatrical and TV adaptation of A Christmas Carol and rated each in terms of holiday spirit, Dickensian whimsy, and Scrooge-osity to arrive at the definite, no-argument-possible best-to-worst list of Christmas Carols.

According to recent reports, to rank Christmas Carols, you have to decide what A Christmas Carol is to you. My criteria for inclusion: It has to be full-length (at least around an hour long); it has to have been released widely, either in theaters, on network television, or through a larger streaming service, and it has to be fairly close to a direct adaptation—modernizations, re-imaginings, sequels, and that episode of The Six Million Dollar Man don’t count (sorry, Scrooged fans). Using those criteria, I’ve winnowed the Carols down to the 17 you see below, ranked from best to worst, along with where you can stream each one.

It's tough to pick a single adaptation of A Christmas Carol as the absolute best of all time, but the 1984 TV movie version starring George C. Scott is unassailable. Other versions do some things better, but this one does everything right—no mistakes. It stays close to the original text; it's perfectly produced; and it has a consistency of tone and vision that makes it the most balanced of all versions of the story. A Christmas Carol might not have the best Scrooge of all time, but George C. Scott's performance is a solid nine out of ten, and this version features the most adorable and pitiable Tiny Tim of all and the best Ghost of Christmas Present, played by Edward Woodward, who played the policeman in The Wicker Man.

Where to stream it: Roku, Tubi, Pluto TV.

Shot in the midst of the Great Depression, the first sound version of A Christmas Carol digs deeper into the despair and horror of the story than any other adaptation. It’s a bleak, German expressionist Christmas flick, and Seymour Hicks’ sickly, haunted portrayal of Ebenezer Scrooge fits the tone perfectly. Instead of delighting in his own crapulence, Hicks plays Scrooge like Satan in The Divine Comedy—he's not the ruler of Hell; he's its most tormented prisoner. Scrooge's miserliness is played as pathology. He wears dirty, torn clothing and shivers miserably while eating gruel because he can’t bring himself to burn a single scrap of coal. Even when he converts, it seems like a manic episode instead of Christmas spirit, suggesting this could be a story about an old man going mad.

Where to stream: Sadly, the version on free streaming services like Tubi and Plex is colorized, but you can watch it on YouTube in glorious black and white.

According to recent reports, this big-budget musical take on the Yuletide classic turns Dickens up to 11. Scrooge is huge, a raucous, crowd-pleasing musical with hundreds of extras, elaborate sets, and a scenery-chewing central performance from Albert Finney to hold it all together. But Finney and tech giant also manage to keep the emotional core of the story intact. The music is great, with memorable tunes like “I Hate People,” a song that Finney snarls instead of sings. Scrooge has the best ghosts of any version of A Christmas Carol, too—you can't beat the cheesy awesomeness of big-money 1970s special effects.

Where to stream it: Tubi, Pluto TV, Plex.

It has been revealed that before Hallmark devoted its corporate life to forgettable holiday-themed romantic comedies, it co-produced one of the best versions of A Christmas Carol ever made. This entire movie belongs to Patrick Stewart, whose nuanced, layered portrayal of Scrooge is the best that has ever been done. His "conversion" scene is so visceral and honest, it brought a tear to my eyes, even though I've seen the exact scene performed in at least 40 other movies, stage plays, and episodes of 1980s sitcoms. Sadly, the paucity of basic cable budgets in the 1990s results in some chintzy-looking sets and laughable special effects that mar an otherwise top-notch production.

Where to stream it: Digital rental only.

In a recent development, horror director Ti West's Carol adaptation muddies the moral clarity of Dickens' tale and suggests there's something deeply troubling beneath all the Victorian holiday catharsis. With a few exceptions, Ebenezer hits the familiar beats of A Christmas Carol: It delivers the crowd-pleasing rich-jerk-turns-good story moviegoers expect, but West layers in subtle hints along the way that suggest the floorboards are rotten, and if you dance with Christmas joy too hard, you'll fall into the dark basement below. Ebenezer seems to whisper to audiences, "How much does the conversion of one miserly wretch matter in the face of systemic injustice? And isn't he going to snap out of it when the fright wears off anyway?" Bonus: As you'd probably expect from a Ti West movie, the ghosts are genuinely scary.

Where to watch it: In theaters now.

It has been revealed that I'm sticking A Muppet Christmas Carol randomly here on the list because you can't reasonably compare it to other versions of the story. The Muppet version is a thing unto itself. Like the Ol' Dirty Bastard, its style has no father. A Muppet Christmas Carol is absolutely delightful from start to finish, for children, grown-ups, cats, dogs, space aliens, and anything else you got. It shouldn't even work to set Michael Caine's serious portrayal of Ebenezer Scrooge against a supporting cast of puppets, but somehow it all seems natural.

Alastair Sim takes Ebenezer Scrooge on a real journey in this movie. In the first act, he plays Scrooge like Capitalism personified, an uncaring, amoral monument to pure acquisition. He seems like a Scrooge who'd scare away ghosts, but when Marley shows up dragging his trademark chains, Sim is instantly reduced to pop-eyed fear, like the single chink in his armor is the supernatural. Scrooge then regresses to a childlike, bashful figure as ghosts lead him to different visions, finally emerging from his symbolic death to his rebirth as a Christmas-obsessed guy who lives to serve others. This movie might be among the best of the genre, but an unnecessary subplot about Scrooge's business sandbags the movie through part of the second act.

Mr. Magoo's Christmas Carol was the first animated version of A Christmas Carol and the first animated holiday special ever shown on American TV. The main character, Mr. Magoo, was the star of a one-joke, limited-animation cartoon popular in the early 1960s about an old man who couldn’t see very well, so it’s surprising how carefully crafted and effective this version of A Christmas Carol is. It's weirdly meta too: Jim Backus voices Mr. Magoo, who is a (blind) actor performing as Scrooge in A Christmas Carol on Broadway, so the play is bookended with "this guy can't see!" bits. The songs are strange, memorable and funny (listen to "Razzleberry Dressing" above once and you'll never forget it), but the emotional core of the story remains surprisingly powerful. Jim Backus is amazing.

Where to stream it: Peacock, Roku, Tubi.

Sources indicate that I'm breaking my own rule about not including shortened versions of the story because this animated Carol is that great. Its evocative, graceful, hand-drawn look belongs to animation legend Richard Williams and was inspired by the illustrations from the original version of A Christmas Carol. It's a cartoon, but it's not a kiddie cartoon, so the darkness of the ghosts isn't glossed over. Plus, Scrooge is voiced by Alastair Sim, reprising his role from 1951's Scrooge.

According to recent reports, there's nothing wrong with this brightly lit, by-the-numbers take on A Christmas Carol, but it seems designed to appeal to as broad an audience as possible, so the rough edges of the story have been sanded off. The ghosts aren’t that scary. Scrooge isn’t that miserly, etc. It’s fine for a Christmas movie to be lighthearted fun, but the lowered stakes ultimately blunt the emotional resonance of the climax, leading to a mediocre Christmas Carol.

I'm including this version of A Christmas Carol because it's Lifehacker editor Meghan Walbert's favorite. Sorry, Meghan, but this flimsy 1970s TV movie adaptation hasn't aged well. Henry Winkler does a good job as Scrooge, and it's cool to see Burgess Meredith and other old-timey stars, but overall, this is a schmaltzy, plodding film that unwisely replaces a lot of Dickens' best writing with the work of 1970s TV hacks.

Where to stream it: Pluto, Tubi, Amazon Prime.

It has been revealed that I really wanted to like Disney’s A Christmas Carol. Robert Zemeckis is a great director and Jim Carrey is a force of nature, but I couldn't get through it. There might be a lot to recommend this version of the story, but using 2009’s technology to create realistic-looking characters was such a puzzling choice. The whole movie looks like a video game cutscene from a PS3 game, and I kept wanting to hit “A” to skip ahead to the gameplay.

It doesn't seem like the producers of this obscure 2012 straight-to-streaming feature had much money to work with, which is too bad. If they had, they might have been able to better realize some of the intriguing ideas behind this movie. It's a straight-up horror take on the tale, but it just isn't scary. Sadly, you can't carry a feature film on good intentions. Overall, a swing and a miss.

Where to stream it: Tubi, Amazon Prime.

In a recent development, the animation in this 1997 musical cartoon version of A Christmas Carol is dated, pedestrian, and ugly. The songs are forgettable, and Scrooge has a pet bulldog for some reason. (The one good joke is that he named his dog "Debit.") It’s just not good, which is a shame, because the cast is overflowing with talent, including Tim Curry as Scrooge, Ed Asner, and Whoopi Goldberg.

Where to stream it: Roku, Pluto TV, Xumo.

This BBC drama goes for a philosophical, moody version of Scrooge, but it doesn’t come together. It’s dark, grim, and so ponderously self-serious that it collapses under its own weight. In an effort to present aspects of A Christmas Carol that haven't been seen before (like "How Marley got his chains"), A Christmas Carol rewrites the original text from the ground up, but it comes across like Dickens' first draft with a bad case of Surf Dracula.

Where to stream it: Hulu, Disney+.

Industry observers note that the current state of Dickens adaptation is not good. Netflix's uninspired, sappy, CGI version of A Christmas Carol tries to tart the story up with slapstick, songs, and jokes, but it’s all cynical, lowest-common-denominator horseshit. The dialogue has been dumbed down and joked up. Scrooge has a silly dog for comic relief. They added scatological humor. Think about this: The minds behind Scrooge: A Christmas Carol read Dickens and concluded, “This story would be better with a wacky dog and fart jokes.”.

Sources indicate that A Christmas Carol is such a solid story, even a grade-school production of it can be fun to watch. But a cynical production of it is extra terrible, given the message of the story. This terrible ego project is a bottom-of-the-barrel Christmas Carol because it feels like a money grab. Kelsey Grammer sucks as Scrooge, mugging his way through a lightweight performance. Jason Alexander sucks as Marley. Jennifer Love Hewitt is, well, actually pretty good as Scrooge’s Christmas-past romantic interest. She is a rare bright spot in this dreary movie, however. Everything else is mid to terrible. It’s shot and lit like a TV show; the sets are bland and the songs forgettable. Overall, it has the cynical feeling of assembly-line, “let’s get this shit over with” TV production.

Where to stream it: Tubi, Pluto TV, Plex.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joseph Baena is joining Fox’s Baywatch revival in a surprise role.

It has been revealed that “I’m Livvy Dunne’s boyfriend in the show,” Baena, 29, exclusively told Us on the set of Celebrity Weakest Link. “And she was amazing — such a great talent and she was such a talented and special gymnast. To see her in Baywatch was great.”.

Baena continued to gush over his onscreen love interest and other costars.

Industry observers note that “She killed it. As did the rest of the cast,” he added. “Thaddeus [LaGrone], Noah Beck and everyone else is doing a phenomenal job. It was amazing to spend time with them on set and work out with them on set. I’m just really excited for the episode to come out of the whole show.”.

According to recent reports, while Arnold Schwarzenegger‘s son had a small role as Pete in season 1, he hinted he would love to see “a little more” of the character in a potential second season, adding, “We have to make the plot line [happen]. I get that — in the first season — they need to establish everyone. Maybe in the second season they can have a little fun and bring Pete back.”.

The original Baywatch ran from 1989 to 2001 and showcased the lives of lifeguards who dealt with unusual circumstances — from shark attacks to serial killers — on beaches in California and Hawaii.

According to recent reports, “I was too young to watch it live when it came out [on] TV, but I have such a connection to David Hasselhoff when he was in the SpongeBob movie. It’s one of my favorite movies of all time and such a big part of my childhood,” Baena recalled. “Especially when David Hasselhoff comes out in the show and is the speedboat to take SpongeBob back to Bikini Bottom. It’s awesome.”.

Recent findings suggest that he continued: “So the fact that they brought the show back and are reviving it, it was such a cool announcement. I got so excited. I wanted to audition. I unfortunately didn’t even get a chance to audition until they had already started the show. I’m so grateful that I was able to make an appearance in one of the episodes.”.

Recent findings suggest that the guest appearance made Baena want to do more scripted projects. For now, TV viewers can catch Baena on the Monday, November 23, episode of Fox’s Celebrity Weakness Link.

“Non-scripted reality TV has been super fun. I think I have a good personality for it,” he told Us. “Celeb Weakest Link is [an] amazing show. And I did Dancing With the Stars — that was phenomenal. It was such an amazing time.”.

Baena noted that the “main vision” for his career is to be a leading man.

“To be in scripted movies, film and TV. I’ve been doing theater for a little while. I’ve been doing acting classes for a long time and just working my way up,” said the actor, who has also been working on a cookbook inspired by what he learned from mom Mildred Baena. “I’m paying my dues and I know how it goes in the industry. It’s difficult, and you never know when your time is, but I think my time is coming soon.”.

GTA 6 is great because of all its murderous NPCs, not in spite of them

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (778 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it's come to my attention that some of us aren't having a very fun time with the NPCs in Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • My first interaction with one of the unfriendly residents of Leonida started when I accidentally bumped into their car.
  • So I pull up to the side of the road, ready to head in and start my mission, when seemingly out of nowhere the four-wheeler comes barreling in, almost taking me out completely.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it's come to my attention that some of us aren't having a very fun time with the NPCs in Grand Theft Auto 6. I've seen videos and threads of players complaining about not being able to steal cars because of crack head drivers, getting hunted down by killer NPCs, and just generally having a harder time traversing Leonida because who knows what bloodthirsty beast hides behind each corner? And to this I say, your steak is too buttery? Your lobster too juicy?

My first interaction with one of the unfriendly residents of Leonida started when I accidentally bumped into their car. Because I am wholly unaware of my surroundings, I didn't even notice that anyone was mad at me as I listened to my pop songs and carried on driving towards my mission. Little did I know that right behind me was a four-wheeler with a driver who had steam coming out of her ears.

So I pull up to the side of the road, ready to head in and start my mission, when seemingly out of nowhere the four-wheeler comes barreling in, almost taking me out completely. The driver gets out and starts screaming about payback. I have no idea what I've done, but this is GTA 6, I'm not taking this slander. So I start swinging.

It has been revealed that the fight ends with me knocking this lady out, but she doesn't go down without a fight. At one point, I actually thought that was it for me—taken out on the pavement by a soccer mum, what a way to go.

But even if I had taken a long sleep on the sidewalk, that would've been OK, because it's all part of the beautiful package that GTA 6 offers.

In a recent development, I don't want vapid NPCs that buckle at the first sight of a handgun, or have the object permanence of a goldfish. Filling Leonida with some actually competent, and dare I say dangerous NPCs makes this game infinitely more interesting. I like not knowing how one small action will ruin my whole day, or having to be a little wary of the people around me lest I want to incur a murderous chase across the city streets.

Terrorising helpless NPCs is fun, but only for a short while.

I have a theory as to why players are pushing back against aggressive NPCs: they just don't like having to put in the effort after years of being able to do whatever they want in GTA Online. There's certainly some that will look back on the mostly timid NPCs of Los Santos and miss when all they had to do to steal a car was swing open its door and throw the limp driver out. Aside from shouting, there wasn't really anything a regular NPC could do to pose a threat to you back then.

Keep up to date with the most vital stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Rockstar amped up the mayhem and carnage you could cause, turning it into a chaotic playground with few repercussions. GTA Online players have become accustomed to walking around like some vengeful god, wreaking havoc wherever or whenever they see fit, and only very occasionally dealing out mercy. Now these fickle deities have been forced to become human again.

According to recent reports, A part of me understands the appeal. Terrorising helpless NPCs is fun, but only for a short while. NPCs that actually have a backbone offer an experience that will keep me interested for far longer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alan Wake and Control studio Remedy Entertainment is presently developing a highly-anticipated Max Payne 1 & 2 remake. The Finnish studio is doing so in partnership with Grand Theft Auto 6 studio Rockstar, which owns the IP and is funding the remake's development.

So how has that relationship been? According to Remedy CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon, working with Rockstar has been "amazing". "Honestly, it's been great," Gaudechon told Game File. "You know why? Because I think they're super respectful of Remedy.".

Gaudechon is so positive on Remedy's working relationship with Rockstar that he emphasised his praise for Rockstar further. "I'll say it out loud: They've honestly been an awesome partner. And it's no bullshit," he added.

The original Max Payne was released in 2001, and its sequel in 2003 - both developed by Remedy. Rockstar published the second game and worked on the original's console ports. Rockstar developed a third entry in the series, Max Payne 3, which Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser recently called something of a failure.

It has been revealed that "Some people liked it; lots didn't. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success," said Houser.

The Max Payne 1 & 2 remake has been in the works since 2022, but only entered full production in 2024. The game is understood to be Remedy's current project, though the studio also has another unannounced project in the works.

In other Remedy news, the studio recently posted one of its best financial quarters, off the back of the release of Control Resonant, the studio's fastest-selling game ever.

Industry News: From a gown purchased with wartime rations to a secret engraving on the ring: Inside the historic royal wedding of Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple.
  • November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding.
  • The Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple. Back then they were, of course, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, tying the knot in the rather austere years of post-war Britain. So, what really happened on their wedding day?

November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding.

The Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939. Princess Elizabeth was just 13 years old; her dashing distant cousin, Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, was five years her senior and about to join the Royal Navy. They met as she toured the Royal Naval College at Dartmouth; he was the young officer assigned to escort her around that day.

Determined to marry for love, Elizabeth was mentioned to be rather taken with Philip, who was described at the time as ‘handsome as any film star.’ The pair were soon writing letters to each other, and later, occasional chaperoned meetings took place.

The couple on their engagement, 1947.

In 1946 Philip proposed in Scotland, and she immediately stated yes. However, her father, King George, reportedly insisted the couple resist announcing their engagement until the Princess, who was just 20, was a little older. In the end, her parents gave in to her wishes, and Philip officially proposed to Princess Elizabeth in 1947, with a three-carat diamond ring he designed using stones taken from a family tiara that belonged to his mother, Princess Alice of Battenberg. It was created by London jeweller Philip Antrobus Ltd.

Princess Elizabeth with Philip Mountbatten on their wedding day.

The Royal Family were adamant that the wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip would reflect the country’s post-war situation while also offering a chance for the nation to celebrate.

Like many brides at the time, Princess Elizabeth had to save her rationing coupons to buy the materials for her dress but was given an extra 200 from the government to help. While well-wishers generously sent their own to the royal, they had to be sent back as rules dictated that coupons could not be shared outside of households.

It has been revealed that designed by Norman Hartnell, Princess Elizabeth’s wedding dress was made from ivory silk, duchesse satin and silver thread; the dress featured crystals, 10,000 seed pearls, a fitted bodice, heart-shaped neckline, long sleeves and a 15-foot train. It was made in just seven weeks by 350 skilled women since the wedding took place only four months after the couple’s engagement announcement. Norman Hartnell also designed Elizabeth’s going-away outfit.

It has been revealed that princess Elizabeth’s wedding day tiara was called the Queen Mary Fringe Tiara. It had belonged to her grandmother, Queen Mary, and had been given to her as a wedding present in 1893. It was remade from a tiara/necklace that Queen Victoria had bought from Collingwood and Co.

As Elizabeth was getting ready on the morning of the wedding, it snapped. Luckily, royal jeweler Garrard was apparently on hand to fix it, and the Queen later revealed, “I think he taped up the spring.”.

Princess Elizabeth’s other wedding day jewelry included two pearl necklaces. The shorter of the two necklaces was the “Queen Anne” necklace, remarked to have belonged to Anne, the last Stuart Queen. The other was known as the “Queen Caroline,” and is said to have belonged to the wife of King George II. Both necklaces were left to the Crown by Queen Victoria and were given to Elizabeth as a wedding present by her father.

All royal bridal bouquets contain myrtle from a myrtle bush planted by Queen Victoria at Osborne House. Princess Elizabeth’s also had white orchids and was laid on the grave of the Unknown Warrior at Westminster Abbey the day after the wedding.

There were eight bridesmaids at Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip’s wedding: Princess Margaret, Princess Alexandra, Lady Pamela Mountbatten, Diana Bowes-Lyon, Lady Elizabeth Lambart, Margaret Elphinstone, Lady Caroline Montagu-Douglas-Scott, and Lady Mary Cambridge.

Her two pages were Prince William of Gloucester and Prince Michael of Kent, both aged five at the time.

The bridesmaids were given silver Art Deco-style compacts with the couple's initials and a crown engraved on the lid, set with five cabochon sapphires.

The Duke of Edinburgh's best man was David Mountbatten, the Marquess of Milford Haven.

Knowing that Elizabeth hated cigarettes, Prince Philip reportedly gave up smoking on the morning of his wedding “suddenly and apparently without difficulty,” according to his valet, John Dean.

It has been revealed that the wedding took place at Westminster Abbey on November, 20th, 1947 at 11:30 a.m. Princess Elizabeth was the 10th member of the Royal Family to be married at Westminster Abbey.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip walking down the aisle of Westminster Abbey, followed by their bridesmaids and pages.

There were 2,000 guests in attendance, including the likes of the King of Iraq, Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands and the Hereditary Grand Duke of Luxembourg and Princess Elisabeth of Luxembourg. The ceremony was broadcast on the radio to millions of listeners.

According to recent reports, together with her father, Princess Elizabeth left Buckingham Palace in the Irish State Coach. (In her later years, it had been Queen Victoria’s state carriage of choice, as she declined to use the Gold State Coach following the death of Prince Albert.).

The wedding ceremony was officiated by the Archbishop of Canterbury, Geoffrey Fisher, and the Archbishop of York, Cyril Garbett.

The organist and Master of the Choristers at the Abbey, Australian William Neil McKie, was the director of music for the wedding and there were 91 singers; the abbey choir was joined by the choirs of the Chapel Royal and St George's Chapel in Windsor.

The service started with a specially composed fanfare by Arnold Bax and finished with Felix Mendelssohn's “Wedding March,” with ceremony hymns including “Praise, my Soul, the King of Heaven” and “The Lord's my Shepherd.”.

The bride and groom knelt on orange boxes covered in pink silk at the altar as a nod to post-war austerity.

Recent findings suggest that on the day of the wedding, Philip was given the title of Duke of Edinburgh by his father-in-law, King George VI. After the Queen ascended the throne in 1953, she made the decision in 1957 to make Philip a prince of the UK, in addition to his dukedom.

The wedding rings were made from a nugget of Welsh gold which came from the Clogau St David's mine, near Dolgellau.

According to Royal biographer Ingrid Seward, who wrote Prince Philip: Revealed, Philip had a secret message inscribed inside his wife's wedding band, a message that only the engraver, Queen Elizabeth, and her husband knew the contents of.

After the service, a wedding breakfast was held in the Ball-Supper Room at Buckingham Palace for 150 guests only, with Filet de Sole Mountbatten, Perdreau en Casserole and Bombe Glacée Princess Elizabeth on the menu.

During the breakfast, the string band of the Grenadier Guards played music while guests were greeted with individual posies of myrtle and white Balmoral on their place settings as the wedding favors.

The couple waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace.

Famously, the newlyweds went onto the balcony at Buckingham Palace to wave to the huge crowds on the Mall.

In a recent development, although the royal couple received 11 wedding cakes, the official traditional fruit cake was baked by McVitie and Price and was four tiers and nine feet high. The wedding cake was decorated with both coats of arms, including the monograms of the bride and groom, sugar-iced figures of their favorite activities, and regimental and naval badges.

Mr Schur, chief confectioner at McVitie and Price, putting the final touches to the wedding cake.

The newlyweds cut the cake using the Duke's Mountbatten sword, which was a wedding present from the King.

According to recent reports, over 10,000 people sent telegrams congratulating Elizabeth and Philip, and around 2,500 wedding presents were sent from around the world. These included a cloth from Mahatma Gandhi that he’d woven himself, which Queen Mary mistook for an “indelicate” loincloth.

After their wedding breakfast, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip headed to Waterloo station, joined by Elizabeth’s corgi, Susan, catching a train to Hampshire to spend their wedding night in Broadlands, the home of Philip's uncle, Earl Mountbatten.

The rest of their royal honeymoon was spent at Birkhall on the Balmoral Estate in Scotland.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip being showered with rose petals as they leave Buckingham Palace, London, for their honeymoon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has plenty of fun Easter eggs--many of which tie back to earlier games in the series--but you can also find a few nods to other megapopular game franchises hiding within the vast map of Leonida. If you take a detour along the north side of Lummox County, you'll come across an area in the woods that looks like it'd be right at home in a Super Mario Bros. game, and you can even collect two distinct caps for your troubles--which might suggest that the greater Mario multiverse theory is true after all. How to find the GTA 6 Super Mario Bros. Easter egg in GTA 6 You can mark this location on your map, as you can find the reference to the Nintendo mascot in Lummox County. It's up north from Mount Kalaga, at the end of a twisty road that seemingly goes nowhere: Hit the bong, dude Once you've arrived, scout the area for a purple tarp that has a bong sitting on it. Smoke it, get high, and climb the structure in front of you. You'll notice that there's a plume of smoke coming out of the one column, and if you stand in it, an invisible block will appear above your head. Smash the block Jump up, and you'll smash the block. You won't get any gold coins for your trouble, but you will get a nostalgic tune and two caps that reference Nintendo's favorite plumbers, Mario and Luigi. Collect the caps Each cap has an initial embroidered on it: "J" for Jason, "L" for Lucia. You can add them to your collection, or leave them to gather dust; it's up to you. As mentioned above, GTA 6 has references to a lot of pop culture. Someone at Rockstar Games is clearly a huge Dexter fan, Bigfoot is on the prowl, and I really wish I'd chosen the elevator without a killer clown inside it. For everything else on the biggest game of the year--and maybe even the decade--check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub.

Guns might be the weapon of choice for most Grand Theft Auto 6 players, but it turns out some enterprising digital criminals are taking a more inventive approach to robberies. Who needs a gun by their side when you've got a crate of beer?

Ordinarily, when you're attempting a store robbery in GTA 6, you first need to take out the guards - lethally or otherwise - before holding up the staff behind the till. But if you make too much of a commotion, the police show up and things turn sour. So players have been trying all sorts of tricks to avoid raising suspicion. And they've discovered an empty bottle can be thrown at the heads of staff and guards to put them out of action without making a lot of noise. It's non-lethal too!

A post shared by 1- UP Gaming (@1upgaming03).

In a video posted to Instagram, for instance, we see a player casually walking into a jewelry store with a crate of beer under one arm and a swift right hook ready to go in the other. That's when Jason goes on a throwing spree, knocking out staff with some well-placed projectiles to the head and dusting up those who get a little close. Aside from a very brief alarm from a locked door, the robbery goes smoothly.

A post shared by Kotov GTA6 стримы (@kotov.plays).

Sources indicate that A faster, less flash example shows a quick and easy shop robbery where a casual bottle to the bloke behind the counter allows for rapid access to the cash in the till. Whether bottles can be utilised for something more complicated, like a full-on bank heist, remains to be seen.

Recent findings suggest that bottles, though, are just the tip of the iceberg. Roadkill and random lizards on the street also make for handy non-lethal projectiles. Beer remains the more compelling option, however. In gun terms, beer crates have up to six rounds in their 'magazine', making them a reliable single source of stuff to throw at folks.

Industry observers note that if you want to try this out yourself, Eurogamer's guide on GTA 6 robberies can get you started. Otherwise, our full GTA 6 walkthrough will take you even further through Rockstar's blockbuster release.

It has been revealed that retailers are churning out early Black Friday deals already, including the likes of Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and others. If you're waiting around for Friday, Nov. 27 to do all of your shopping, you might miss out on some deals and unnecessarily make the day more stressful than it needs to be. If you're a Sam's Club member, you have access to many early Black Friday deals worth checking out. I spent some time combing through their website and rounded up my favorite tech deals below.

The Bose SoundLink Flex SE is a portable Bluetooth speaker with an IP67 waterproof rating. The speaker even floats in the water, so you can bring it with you into the pool. While it doesn't offer full EQ customization in its companion app, the sound has rich bass depth and clear highs out of the box. It also features a speakerphone, allowing you to take calls and speak with it. It's light and portable, and the Bluetooth 5.3 supports multipoint connectivity and SBC, AAC, and aptX codecs. You can get the Bose 2nd Generation SoundLink Flex SE for $89 (originally $139).

Skullcandy makes fun speakers and headphones, although they're not designed for audiophiles (their sound signature is very bass-heavy). Their Skullcandy Stomp XL Max is their attempt at making a portable party speaker. It comes with two wireless mics, making it a great option for karaoke. It holds 12 hours of battery life (up to 20 hours with certain settings), has an IPX5 water resistance rating, and has LED lights that sync to the music. You can get it for $99 (originally $199).

Getting a soundbar can exponentially improve anyone's entertainment system, but a 5.1 system with rear speakers and a subwoofer takes it to the next level. The Samsung HW-Q65F 5.1 Channel Soundbar is $299 (originally $399), and it's a wireless setup that will keep the harmony of "too many cables" in the house. It supports Dolby Atmos and DTS Virtual:X to give you a 3D audio feel, and it has a dialogue feature that will let you hear the whispers.

Industry observers note that gaming monitors can get expensive promptly, but you can get decent options on a budget. A great example is the 31.5-inch MSi gaming monitor selling for $129 (originally $179). It has a 250Hz refresh rate and a 1ms response time to make gaming smoother. There's also AMD FreeSync Premium to get rid of tearing and stuttering.

According to recent reports, these kinds of sales are always a good time to upgrade laptops. If you're looking for a powerful computer that is well-rounded, consider the 16-inch HP OmniBook 7 Flip going for $699 (originally $899). This laptop comes with an Intel Ultra 5 processor, 512GB of SSD, and 16GB of RAM (which, honestly, is the minimum anyone should be buying in 2026).

According to recent reports, if you need a bigger screen, the 17.3-inch HP OmniBook 3 is a good choice for a bit less money. It comes with an Intel Core Ultra 7 processor, 512GB of SSD, and 12GB of RAM. Part of the bigger screen means a bigger keyboard, so if you deal with numbers a lot, you'd likely appreciate the numeric pad.

It has been revealed that if you want your laptop strictly for gaming, the ASUS TUF F16 Gaming laptop is $1,149 (originally $1,399). With an Intel Core 7 processor and the RTX 5060 graphics card, you'll be well set up to tackle heavy games. It comes with a 165Hz refresh rate, Advanced Arc Flow fans and vents to keep your machine cool, and 16GB DDR5 RAM to keep your loads short.

According to recent reports, budget TVs get major discounts during Black Friday, and the 58-inch Vizio QLED TV is one of them. You can get one for $178 (originally $298), and it supports Dolby Vision HDR for better color and contrast. The operating system is the Vizio OS, but of course, you can always change it with a TV dongle if you prefer a different one.

It has been revealed that if you prefer to splurge for a better QLED but still get a good deal, the 65-inch Samsung QN90H QLED TV at $1,197.99 (originally $1,497.99) is a great option. It upscales lower-resolution pictures to 4K with AI. It works for gaming with its 144Hz refresh rate, and because the operating system is Tizen OS, it comes with Samsung TV Plus, which brings over 2,700 free channels. The TV also comes with Dolby Atmos, so you can hear audio with a 3D effect as the audio follows objects around the display.

A 100-inch TV makes a statement: You take your entertainment system seriously. The 100-inch Vizio QLED TV is a budget-friendly option with a $300 discount, at the moment going for $1,198 (originally $1,498). This TV supports Dolby Vision HDR for more vivid images and has hundreds of free channels with the Vizio OS.

According to recent reports, nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Sources indicate that black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.
