In a recent development, halide 3.4 is out today as the latest update to the pro camera app. The update adds several newly introduced features, including a larger viewfinder for iPhone Duo and more.

According to recent reports, the new Halide upgrade also lets you use the outer screen on iPhone Duo as a live preview or a fill flash. It brings back a few camera tools from Halide Mark II as well.

Lux Optics first added iPhone Duo support in October with Halide 3.3. With the phone fully open, the initial iPhone Duo revision let you review your most recent photo alongside the live viewfinder.

Today’s new XL mode gives you the option to swap the photo preview for a larger viewfinder. Controls on both sides enable two-handed shooting.

While the Duo is open, the outer screen can mirror Halide’s camera controls or show a full-screen viewfinder without controls. The second option lets the person you’re photographing see how you’ve framed the shot.

In a recent development, in low light, Halide can use the outer screen as a fill flash. That gives you a softer source of light for portraits, and Halide’s developers recommend turning the screen brightness all the way up before taking the photo.

Industry observers note that halide also now places the histogram along the Duo’s crease. The enhancement revises the Photo Lab interface for editing with the Duo half open as well.

On other iPhones, Halide 3.4 restores the color and luminance histograms and the shutter timer from Mark II.

Halide Mark III launched back in May with a redesigned camera and the upcoming Photo Lab editor. Recent updates added RAW-only capture in 3.1 and Aperture Priority for iPhone 18 Pro in 3.2. Halide Mark III version 3.4 is available now on the App Store.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27 gave AirPods Pro a variety of upcoming features, but there’s another addition that’s easy to miss: a convenient new setting in Control Center for Adaptive Audio.

Several AirPods models offer excellent Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency modes—especially AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179).

But Adaptive Audio is another option you may or may not have tried. The feature aims to blend the strengths of both ANC and Transparency in a single mode.

And in iOS 27, Apple added a new setting to let you conveniently fine-tune Adaptive Audio to your preferences.

It has been revealed that while wearing AirPods, open Control Center on your iPhone and tap the volume slider, then hit ‘Listening Mode’ in the bottom-left corner. Here you’ll see the standard listening mode options.

Newly introduced in iOS 27 though, when ‘Adaptive’ is selected, you can now use a Liquid Glass slider to adjust whether the mode lets in more or less external noise.

Slide it to the left and Adaptive Audio will more closely resemble Transparency, while sliding it to the right makes it cancel out more noise.

According to recent reports, you can also move the new slider incrementally to achieve exactly your ideal balance of Transparency and Noise Cancellation. It’s not limited to just a few preset options.

This Control Center slider is available on all AirPods models that support Adaptive Audio.

Do you ever use Adaptive Audio, and if so, have you adjusted it at all? Let us know in the comments.

According to recent reports, does Frank Carter have Rotten luck? For the past year and a half, the 42-year-old British punk singer whose credits include Gallows and his solo work fronting the Rattle Snakes, has served as the singer for the Sex Pistols. Most recently, the band performed a tour celebrating the 50th anniversary of its only proper album, Never Mind the Bollocks. But it seems the bollocks have come swinging back like a pendulum for Carter since the Pistols have confirmed there’s no future for Carter after the next run of U.K. reveals.

Sources indicate that “It’s been a glorious ride with Frankie baby, we’ve loved every minute,” guitarist Steve Jones told Kerrang! “The shows were spectacular and of course, a major shout out to all the fans. Without you lot, it’s nothing. This is not the end of the Pistols… but let’s see what happens.”.

Carter’s statement also expresses several emotions that are easy to never mind with the Sex Pistols: gratitude, optimism, and hope. “As a young kid growing up on Sex Pistols, the scale of the opportunity to step into one of the most iconic roles in music history was not lost on me,” he said. “I never thought for a second that three highlights to help save Bush Hall would turn into all this. To Steve, Paul [Cook, drums] and Glen [Matlock, bass], thank you for trusting me with such an key task. And thanks to the crew and every fan who’s been smiling, dancing and screaming the words back at me all over the world; it has been a huge honour.

“All good things must come to an end, and I’m really looking forward to celebrating my run with the Pistols one last time around our Bloody Kingdom,” he continued. “As always, I’ll see you in the pit.”.

Carter’s final Anarchy in the U.K. tour (which includes Ireland) with the Pistols will begin on Dec. 4 and end on Dec. 20.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that “I wanted to bring color and life to the world of corridos,” Rey Quinto tells Rolling Stone.
  • Rey Quinto is the stage name of Arturo Herrera Altamirano, who is based in Guadalajara.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The corridos scene often attracts the same tough-talking singers but Rey Quinto is looking to shake things up with some guyliner. In the past year, the rising Mexican star has become a go-to collaborator for heavyweights in the genre like Peso Pluma, Netón Vega, and Luis R. Conriquez who want a touch of his unexpected sound. Now Rey Quinto is stepping into the spotlight with his debut album, the aptly titled Atravesao —  and yes, he’s doing it all with a freshly beat mug.

Industry observers note that “I wanted to bring color and life to the world of corridos,” Rey Quinto tells Rolling Stone. “I’ll be performing in makeup like Prince or Michael Jackson in the Eighties. That’s my persona. Singing corridos in that way is something people won’t expect. It’ll likely draw some criticism, too.”.

Rey Quinto is the stage name of Arturo Herrera Altamirano, who is based in Guadalajara. The first part of his stage name comes from being a fan of the WWE legend Rey Mysterio. Where does the five come from? He has strong ties to the number five, including being born in 2005 during the fifth month of the year, and a love for the Carlos V chocolates.

According to recent reports, after singing as a hobby, Rey Quinto wrote a song at 15 that was inspired by his first major heartbreak. “That’s how I processed my grief,” he recalls. “It was because of that breakup and I thought, ‘Hey, [the song] actually turned out pretty well.” Three years later, he was signed by local label Golden Ink Entertainment.

Rey Quinto was already becoming a hot commodity in corridos in recent years. Vega previously tapped him for the song “Agua de Horchata” in 2025 and Conriquez enlisted him for “Aguas” earlier this year. But Rey Quinto’s career was taken to newly introduced heights when Peso Pluma reached out. The Mexican superstar highlighted interest in a song that he wrote called “Marianita.” At that point, Rey Quinto was keeping his compositions to himself, but it was a different story with Peso. “That one time was an exception,” he says. “Working with him was always a dream of mine. Peso told me, ‘Hey man, I really like your songs, too.’ It was wild.” Peso and Tito Double P adapted “Marianita” into a collaboration with Rey Quinto for their Grammy-nominated album Dinastía. He also hand-picked Rey Quinto to open for their U.S. tour earlier this year. “I have so much respect for [Peso],” Rey Quinto adds. “I learned a lot from him and Tito.”  Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

In a recent development, even Rey Quinto recognizes how much he stands apart in the corridos music scene and how he’s introduced a much-needed, and fierce, makeover. “I drew inspiration from who I am, both inside and out,” he claims. “The real essence of what I’m doing is unconventional just like I am as a person. It’s a risk to go out wearing makeup while singing corridos. Here in Mexico, a lot of people aren’t going to look too kindly on that. Well, since I’m doing this from the heart, it doesn’t bother me. I don’t care what people think.”.

On Atravesao, Rey Quinto brings back a lot of the artists who first gave him a leg up in música mexicana. The daring LP boasts features from Vega on “Los Azules,” Tito Double P on “Increible,” and Conriquez and Clave Especial on “42.” Peso Pluma also joins Rey Quinto on the most left-field song on the album, the title track where Rey Quinto lets his freak flag fly. Industry observers note that “‘Atravesao’ caught Peso’s attention and it really piqued his interest,” he recalls. “He said, ‘This is the first song that we’re going to record.’ From that point on, we started building a closer relationship and making a lot of music together. Honestly, we have a great connection when it comes to creating music. In the studio, things flow smoothly and we really click when we’re bouncing ideas around.”.

Rey Quinto is just getting started, but he’s already making waves with his unorthodox overhaul of corridos. “I want to be someone that lasts my entire life in música mexicana,” he states. “I want to leave a legacy and I want to keep bringing latest and fresh ideas to this genre. In line with the company’s design language, these headphones feature transparent elements and bold, geometric detailing that make them stand out from typical matte-black pairs. But the appeal goes beyond the look. These IP52-rated headphones use 40mm drivers, hybrid ANC, and both USB-C and 3.5mm connectivity. They also support high-res audio via LDAC, while Nothing’s companion app gives you basic and advanced EQ controls for adjusting the sound. Battery life is impressive, too, stretching to 35 hours with ANC on and up to 80 hours with it switched off.

It has been revealed that but the hardware alone doesn’t define the experience—Nothing’s control scheme is what makes these wireless headphones stand out. Instead of touch panels or clunky buttons, you get a satisfying volume scroll wheel (they call it the Roller), a multi-function Paddle for track navigation, and a customizable button that can switch EQ profiles or noise modes. You also get spatial audio and multipoint Bluetooth support, which work well across Android and iOS.

According to recent reports, that said, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. Performance-wise, the ANC handles low-end noise well (think airplane engines and AC hum) but struggles with sharper, unexpected sounds like clanging dishes or chatter nearby. As for its sound profile, it leans towards the punchier side, especially with a bit of EQ tweaking in the app, but you’ll need to put in some effort if you want the best results, notes this PCMag review.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that T he first time I wrote about Chris Christie, he was running for governor in 2009, and I mocked him acidly for running a specious campaign during a time of fiscal crisis. (I noted, cruelly, that he was apparently too heavy to march in a Labor Day parade and had campaigned from the back of a truck, “like the Pope.”) Most politicians I know would never have spoken to me again. Christie, on the other hand, invited me to coffee shortly after he won, and he pressed me to come to Newly introduced Jersey so he could show me his strategy to reverse the state’s rapid decline — a painful plan he sold through dozens of town hall meetings with voters who walked in wanting to throttle him.

That was Christie, as I would come to know him. A prosecutor both by profession and temperament, he sees politics as a giant courtroom and has supreme confidence in his ability to convince you he’s right — undimmed, somehow, by brutal experience.

I’ve sat down with Christie at some very low points (immediately after the existential scandal known as “Bridgegate”) and some better ones (the eve of his first presidential campaign). His odyssey has taken him from the very center of Republican politics to its outer fringe, from nearly running Donald Trump’s White House to emerging as one of its bluntest critics. There have been humiliating moments, some of his own making. But Christie remains, even now, one of his party’s most interesting figures and its most sophisticated communicator. If the post-Trump party is going to have a real debate about whether to return to its intellectual roots or resign itself to the ugly, nativist margins of American life, then it’s hard to imagine Christie won’t have a voice.

I caught up with Christie this time about a week after the midterm elections, at the offices of his small consulting firm in northern Newly introduced Jersey, where the walls of the conference room are adorned with bipartisan mementos. Christie seemed buoyed by the moment. He arrived, cheerful and unhurried, wearing a Knicks sweatshirt from the NBA Finals, as if to signal that things suddenly seemed to be going his way. We talked about the party’s uncertain future, Trump’s weird psychology, Christie’s own worst decisions, and why he can’t stand his former Republican rivals (and especially Jared Kushner). We also talked about why he’s considering a third presidential campaign now, even after the last two cratered. According to recent reports, you’ve been talking for years about how Trump was going to lead your party off a cliff. You feeling vindicated?Sure. Yeah. I mean, absolutely. He can’t control how he really has no moral core of any kind, which of course prevents you from being able to have forgiveness in your heart.

“I don’t think there’s anybody on the political scene of the country who knows [Trump] better than I do.”.

In a recent development, and so when he got power back, I just knew he was going to use that power for two things: to seek vengeance against his enemies and to enrich himself beyond belief. Because it’s all about him. And if you don’t have a moral core, you don’t have a calling to help anyone else. And in fact, when other people benefit from their association with you, you’re angry about it. People have made money off of presidents for centuries, through their association with a president. And most presidents understand that as long as they’re doing it legally, that is part of what happens. This is a guy who, if he’s not getting his cut, it’s personally offensive to him, and he speaks out and tries to hurt those people.

According to recent reports, what do you think the voters were saying here?I think it’s two things. The first and most key one is, it is an absolute personal rejection of him. You don’t see the combination of really high turnout among Democrats and among independents in a midterm and low turnout of Republicans, relatively speaking, without it being a personal rejection of the head of the party. And I think the second thing is, it is another expression of disgust and anger with the way the government system is being operated. But in that instance, everybody feels like they’re being treated the same. The inconvenience is for everyone, and it is for the greater good. And I think the American people complain about some stuff like that, but they don’t act out on it, and they don’t vote on it. So as you point out, you know Trump. What do you think the next two years looks like?It’s going to take a few months for him to get his feet back underneath him. He’s defeated. “I think that we’ll see a really angry last couple of years.”.

Were you the Democrats at this moment, you would not be considering a third impeachment, I take it?Oh, I think it would be the worst idea in the world. You’re not going to remove him. Sources indicate that do you think he’s right in the head now?If you’re asking do I think he is mentally capable of doing the job, the answer I think is yes. The same way we watched Biden, when we elected him at 78 go down the chute and not be capable of going forward for another four years, once he’d gotten to 82. I think Donald Trump we’ll see at the end of this term will be diminished.

In a recent development, you and the Never-Trumpers in the party, you’ve been sounding this alarm for years. It hasn’t achieved very much to this point. Now you have an opening. What’s the initiative? What do you do to get your party back?Talk about yesterday, you’re a loser. You’re not going to change anything. Look, there’s going to be this couple weeks right after the election, where everybody just wants to talk about what happened and that’s fine. Happy to engage in that. But to me, this is about, what’s this party look like going forward. And we better be the party that’s going to take on the major problems. And there are a lot of big problems. We have a healthcare system that’s completely unaffordable, and no one’s willing to do the hard things that need to be done to be able to make it more affordable. If you had a presidency that focused on those things, you would have a breathtaking four years of trying to deal with that stuff. And to me, it’s character, morality, a sense of right and wrong being executed by the person in charge, and a willingness to listen to and compromise with other people who have different ideas. And my party has not shown either of those things. Usually in history, the reaction to a loss like the one we just had is to go in a fresh direction. OK, but doesn’t there need to be a battle plan? There’s going to be a fight inside your party over these principles and these policies, and it takes money and organization. Is there some kind of movement you need to be building?No more committees, thank you. No. No. Money, organization, and movement come from ideas and having a messenger who can express those ideas in a way that both interest and excite people.

In a recent development, but you’ve had these ideas and advanced them for years, and it hasn’t made a dent in the direction of your party. So maybe the ideas by themselves aren’t enough.Well, no. Maybe it’s that it was Trump’s time and not mine. I mean, maybe the people weren’t ready for it yet. Well, now they know it won’t. So my point to you is like, “I don’t know. My ideas and my approach were selling pretty good before he came down the escalator.” I got 60 percent of the vote in a blue state. I ran all the Republican governors, and we got a record number of Republican governors. And then he showed up and he was and is a phenomenon. So these ideas on these issues and how we approach them and articulate them, I was probably too early. I don’t think those ideas are too early now given everything that’s happened.

So you’re considering a third run inside the Republican Party?Yeah.

It didn’t go so well the first two times. It surprised me probably as much as it surprised you.Well, ’16 surprised me; ’24 didn’t surprise me because I knew when I got into that race that there would have to be a lightning strike for it to happen. But my motivation at ’24 was, there has to be someone who’s going to stand up there and say, “This is wrong. This is not who we are. And if we decide to compromise ourselves in this way, we are going to pay a massive price as a party in a country.” And guess what? The bill came due last Tuesday. And everything that the Democrats try to do now that philosophically a number of Republicans will be opposed to? I don’t want to hear your whining about it because you’re making it possible. Your conduct, you’re standing on the sidelines, your capitulating in 2024 made it possible.

Recent findings suggest that the older I get, the more I understand that life is about timing. And so what really happened was that the timing was wrong. And could I have been better? I’m sure I could’ve been in a number of ways. I don’t know that it would’ve made any difference.

You don’t feel Vance or Rubio, the people that are most often talked about now, could take the party in a better direction or would?I probably would ask you a question back. What in their experience tells you that they would? Because there’s nothing there that tells me that.

No, I wouldn’t argue with you.That’s it. I think you can only judge people on what they’ve noted and how they’ve conducted themselves. JD Vance wrote Hillbilly Elegy and became vice president. And I don’t know that that’s the resumé I want for a president of the United States. And I don’t know that I want it to be someone who literally called Trump Hitler and now notes he was the best president of my lifetime. I don’t want somebody who stood up next to Vivek Ramaswamy and said that dragging an obviously disturbed elderly woman out of the car that she lives in and throwing her in front of a camera to talk about her daughter who she hadn’t seen for 50 years, that it disgusts him when people criticize that. Well, that tells me that he has no morality. That’s elder abuse. We put people in jail when I was the U.S. attorney for stuff like that.

Sources indicate that and for Marco, I don’t know how he gets away from the foreign policy failures of this administration. He is both the secretary of state and the national security adviser, and just because he hides from time to time doesn’t mean that he’s not in the middle of it. He’s in that building every day.

Is there anyone out there who would make you say, “Yeah, I’d step aside for that person, or if it’s not me, I hope it’s that candidate.”I mean, I do have some friends out there. I don’t know whether they’re willing to run or not. I mean, I think a guy like Brian Kemp is a really competent, qualified, successful governor and a guy who’s willing to fight Trump and say no to him on a number of things and put his political career at risk for it, and he beat him. And you see what Georgia looks like now without Brian Kemp.

Sources indicate that democratic is how it looks.That’s exactly right. Blue from top to bottom. So Brian’s a guy who I’ve always admired and respected, and I don’t know whether he wants to run or not. We haven’t talked about it. I won’t ever say I’ll step aside for someone because that’s kind of like putting your future in someone else’s hands. As you probably know, from the years we’ve known each other, that’s not my style.

OK. Let’s talk about the history here a little bit because you know I’m not here just to give you softballs. We’ve got to have a conversation.Sure.

You’ve talked about all the people who capitulated, were complicit, but there was that long moment, four years long, where knowing Donald Trump and knowing who he was, you abetted him. In a recent development, “I know why I got fired. Because Jared Kushner had been beating the shit out of me for months.”.

In a recent development, it felt self-interested. So how do you explain it now?Well, I’ll explain it to you really simply. Let’s start at the beginning. When I lost in 2016, I did what has been done throughout the history of modern politics, which is, “OK, I lost. I don’t think I deserve to lose, but I did. He won. Let me go try to make him better.” It was really that simple of a decision. I was like, “He trusts me. We have a relationship that goes back 14 years at that point. Let me go in there and try to make him better.” And that’s what I did. And in the beginning, I think I did have some impact on him. And then he put me in charge of the transition and I thought, “Well, this is a really positive way.” So I got out of the campaign completely by May of 2016. I endorsed it in February. I was out by May, and in May, I became chairman of the transition. And he’s like, “You run that.”.

Recent findings suggest that and I was really given pretty wide berth to do what I wanted to do with the transition, always checking back in with him and with the campaign to make sure that nothing we were doing was contrary to what messaging they wanted to have out there. I put together, pretty much by myself, a group of over 125 people who were in offices in Washington, D.C., who were working every day to put together a whole set of policy initiatives.

I brought in 10 former U.S. attorneys to do the vetting for potential Cabinet and senior staff people. We put together a 12-volume transition. And after he won, I ran the first two transition meetings and then got fired. And I know why I got fired. Because Jared Kushner had been beating the shit out of me for months, from the first time when he came into the office, which was the first time I ever met him.

You knew his father well enough.Yeah, never had met his father either, but I had prosecuted him and knew the family.

Sources indicate that trump later offered you chief of staff.He offered me chief of staff. He offered me secretary of Homeland Security. He offered me secretary of labor. He offered me ambassador to Italy. He offered me ambassador to the Vatican.

Oh, that’s a good one.I didn’t have the money to do it. So he offered me those five jobs, which are all pretty good jobs. Especially when he offered me chief of staff, he couldn’t understand why I wouldn’t take it. And basically the way I explained it to him was, “You and I are going to disagree. I’m going to tell you what I think you need to do and what the truth is. You’re going to get angry with me and fire me. Why don’t we just get to that point now and not go through all the public drama that will have to ensue?” And when I actually said that to him, he laughed and he said, “Yeah, you might be right about that.” He said, “Well, this isn’t the answer I was expecting, but OK.” And really, after I said no to the chief staff thing, we weren’t in touch at all until the spring, summer of 2020, when Covid hit. And he called me to ask me advice on dealing with a crisis like this. And I drove down to the White House to meet with him because the president calls and asks you to help during a national crisis — we had our disagreements, but not about that, at least not about me giving him advice.

And I sat down there one day for five hours, just me and him in the Oval Office. People would wander in from time to time, but we sat there and talked about all this stuff. And it felt to me like early 2016 again. And so then he asked me to prepare him for the debates in 2020, which I did for the first debate. And then he gave me Covid.

Recent findings suggest that and nearly killed you.Yes. I thought, “Well, he didn’t know he had Covid, and so how can I blame him?” Yet he called me when I was in the hospital and asked if I was going to blame him for Covid. I should’ve known then. That was a strange question. I stated, “Well, I don’t know who patient zero is.” I got it. Hope Hicks got it. Bill Stepien got it. Kellyanne Conway got it. I mean, everybody who’s in the room got it. I give you all this background to say: It’s not accurate to say that it was like all sunshine and roses and then all of a sudden it broke. It was deteriorating over time. I was distancing myself over time by not going to work for him. But the break point for me was election night 2020 when I just noted, “I cannot be associated with him. I can’t speak to him. It’s over. I cannot be associated with this in any way.”.

Sources indicate that have you talked to him much since then?We have not spoken since the Friday after the election, 2020. He has sent emissaries to me, which I’ve rejected.

I’m guessing there are two things, just knowing you for a long period of time now, that really piss you off. One is I know you care about the Justice Department. That’s the world you come out of. So I’m betting that the use of the Justice Department as a personal retribution arm and the use of the courts for frivolous criminal prosecutions really gets under your skin.I think it is the single worst thing he’s done in his attack on our government. Yeah. No doubt.

The second thing is Jared Kushner’s out there getting rich off foreign governments while presumably serving the country.Oh, I think it’s wrong, but I don’t really care. The interesting thing about the Kushners is they can put all the lipstick on the pig they want, but everybody knows who they are. In the end, you can call yourself ambassador, you can style yourself a modern day Henry Kissinger or J.P. Morgan or whatever the hell Jared styles himself to be, but everybody knows who you are and what your family is.

Which is what?Which is some of the most reprehensible, dishonest people I’ve ever met in my life. And by the way, it’s not my opinion, as they say. Read the facts.

In a recent development, do you ever wonder how your trajectory would’ve been different absent the Bridgegate thing? It still comes up all the time when your name is mentioned.This is the way I put it, Matt. I’m not responsible for Bridgegate, but I’m accountable for it because it happened on my watch, and I paid as substantial a price as anybody could ever pay for something they didn’t do, but that’s life. And I also got credit for some things that I had nothing to do with either. So I’m not going to say it balances out, but there are examples of both. It’ll be 13 years ago that it broke this January. You never get over it, but I acknowledge what happened in terms of the impact on my career. And yeah, I think it changed the course of history potentially. Yeah.

I don’t spend any time anymore thinking about it. But like you mentioned, people bring it up. So when they bring it up, you’ve got to be prepared to answer about it, because it’s part of your record. It’s part of who you are. It’s part of your public life. It’s an unpleasant part. Look, I dealt for years and will deal, if I do this again going forward, with people obsessing on my weight. Another unpleasant topic. But it’s part of the deal. This is the way life works.

Recent findings suggest that maybe you should have run in 2012. There is a school of thought that the blue sky only opens once.It could wind up being true. I don’t know, but I don’t have any second thoughts about that either because I wasn’t ready.

It has been revealed that because this is Rolling Stone, I have to ask you this. You’re a major fan of Bruce Springsteen, and he has not always been a big fan of yours.Correct.

Have you been able to hug it out?Well, here’s what happened. I guess it was 2022 or 2023, it was right after Covid. Bruce did a show at Barclays, and my older son is a significant fan as well. So he said, “Dad, can we just buy tickets in the pit and go to the show?” And I was like, “Sure.” So me, [my wife] Mary Pat, and Andrew went to the show. And about halfway through the show, I said to them, “Hey, Bruce just pointed at me and smiled.” Well, now you only imagine my family. They mocked me for the rest of the show. They’re like, “No, he didn’t.” I go, “He did.” And then the rest of the show my son goes, “Oh, he just smiled at me! Oh, he just pointed at me!” I mean, they broke my chops for the rest of the show. And I’m like, “Fine. I know what happened.”.

So we leave, get in the car to drive back to Jersey. And it was like, I don’t know, 11:30. My phone rings with a number that I didn’t recognize. So I answered the phone, and it’s Bruce.

Wow.And he’s like, “Hey, man. Gov, I saw you in the audience tonight with Mary Pat and your boy. You guys were having such a great time. You know what I though to myself? I thought to myself, there’s no reason you and I shouldn’t be friends. And you know what? I also know that the biggest reason we’re not is me, not you.” And he said, “So how about this? This is my cellphone number. You use it and call me anytime. There’s any show you ever want to go to anywhere in the world, you just text me and it’s done.” And he said, “Are you going to any of the highlights?” I said, “Yeah, I’ll be at the one at the Prudential Center.” He goes, “Good. Let’s see each other before the show. Let’s take a picture, and I’m going to put it out on social media to let everybody know you and I are cool and I want us to be friends if you’re willing to. And I’m sorry that I contributed to us not being friends.” And I said, “Of course, I’d be happy to be your friend.” And since then, Mary Pat and I have — well, I don’t know how many shows, we’ve been to, but a lot, as his guest all the time. We text back and forth on a regular basis. Talk about things both political and musical and family. It’s now a very good personal relationship.

In a recent development, so which Cabinet department does he get?Yeah, no. I don’t think so.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google is upgrading the Gemini app on Mac with computer use capabilities that can work across local desktop applications and the web.

The existing Task (previously Gemini Spark) functionality in the Mac app could just access local files in conjunction with Connected Apps, like @Gmail or @Google Calendar.

Computer use lets Gemini for Mac click and type on your behalf to accomplish multi-step tasks in local desktop apps and the web, like navigating menus and filling out forms.

In a recent development, gemini works in an “isolated background window with a live preview right in your chat,” while your main screen and cursor remain free to use. On the safety front, you can stop Gemini at any time with one click, while you choose what apps Gemini uses. Google will pause for logins and payments, with confirmation needed for sensitive actions.

In a recent development, many everyday tasks span desktop apps and websites that don’t connect to each other. Computer use handles the tedious steps in the background so you can save time without giving up your screen or cursor.

To use, add @Computer use to your prompt. In Customize > Connectors, you’ll see newly introduced “Desktop” apps like Blender and Autodesk Fusion join the existing Git and Obsidian integrations.

Sources indicate that FTC: We use income earning auto affiliate links. More.

Sources indicate that amazon's Black Friday 2026 sale has brought the Sonos Arc Ultra down to $849 from its usual $1,099, a $250 discount that marks its lowest price yet. PCMag named it the best soundbar of 2024 and gave it an “outstanding” rating in its review. Still, $849 is a lot to spend on a single soundbar, and anyone shopping on a tighter budget will find more affordable picks in our Fire TV soundbar roundup. For more editor-vetted tech deals, check out our comprehensive Black Friday coverage.

Industry observers note that for those who can make room in their budget, the next thing to strategy around is space, since the Arc Ultra measures a little over 46 inches across and weighs about 13 pounds, making it a natural match for a larger TV. Despite all that width, it keeps a low profile at just under three inches tall, so it can sit beneath most screens without blocking the picture, or you can wall-mount it if you would rather keep your TV stand clear. All that size makes room for a 9.1.4-channel layout (a big step up from the original Arc) that gives Dolby Atmos effects more space to spread around and above you. Sonos also added a latest Sound Motion driver that it states doubles the original Arc's bass, giving action scenes real weight without a separate subwoofer, though you can still add a Sub 4 later for more rumble.

It has been revealed that at the other end of the sound spectrum, voices and dialogue come through clearly even at low volumes, and a Speech Enhancement mode lifts them further. Trueplay tuning then adjusts the sound to your room, with a quick version on Android and iOS and a more detailed one for iPhone owners. The biggest drawback is connectivity, since the Arc Ultra has a single HDMI eARC port with no passthrough, which can leave you short on inputs for a console or streaming box, and no optical port. It also lacks DTS:X support, a letdown for some Blu-ray collectors, and voice control is limited to Alexa or Sonos' own assistant, though Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and AirPlay 2 make streaming music from your phone easy.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

S tar’s Revenge II, the second album from the Latest York rock band Star’s Revenge, comes bursting out of the speakers with an overwhelming feeling of freedom. It’s a life-affirming mood, ringing out in every note of Emily Green’s lead guitar and Olive Faber’s wild, yearning vocals. That’s exactly the kind of energy this band wants to tap into, because that’s how they prefer to experience music themselves.

“I don’t think any of us listen to music casually,” indicates Faber, 31. “I’m either sobbing and screaming or hysterically laughing. And when we’re playing the music, it’s almost like this ecstatic joy that’s running through you.”.

“It’s endless, too,” says Green, 24, meaning the world of recorded sound. “That’s one of the best parts of there being eight billion people on the planet. It just feels like endless evidence that human beings can be spectacular, tender creatures.”.

A few days before the album’s Nov. 27 release, the two main songwriters in Star’s Revenge are sitting at a table outside one of their favorite neighborhood pizza spots in Brooklyn alongside bassist Jonny Ceballos, 28, and drummer Christian Billard, 33. All four of them have been playing in bands for years; Faber is the drummer in Sunflower Bean, and Green recently returned home after wrapping Geese’s triumphant fall 2026 tour. As they banter in the midday sun, it’s clear that this group shares a special, easygoing bond.

“It’s the most laid-back band I’ve ever been in,” Ceballos says. “It’s just fun to hang out and eat pizza together.”.

Industry observers note that “Yeah, pizza’s a significant one,” Green agrees between bites of her slice. “It’s the connective tissue of Star’s Revenge.”.

She and Faber first crossed paths in March 2022 in Austin, Texas, where Geese and Sunflower Bean had been booked for the same South by Southwest showcase. “We were playing back-to-back,” Green claims, turning to Faber. “I just thought you were cool.”.

Both of them were at sensitive points in their lives. Faber, who came out to the world as a trans woman that spring, remembers feeling “alone and lost” at the time. (“Oh, me too,” says Green.) They might not have gotten to talking if Sunflower Bean’s manager hadn’t suggested it. “She was like, ‘There’s a trans girl in Geese. You should meet her,'” Faber recalls. They stayed in touch in the months that followed, and in early 2023, they decided to try making music as a duo. Consciously starting a band with someone she’d recently met was a fresh experience for Green, whose friendship with Geese’s Cameron Winter and Max Bassin goes back to grade school. “I’d known Max and Cameron long enough that I don’t remember meeting them, and playing music together just kind of happened naturally,” she says. “This was a bit more definitive. I hadn’t totally experienced that kind of one-on-one creative relationship that ended up being this band.”.

The first album the two of them made as Star’s Revenge was full of messy feelings, woozy melodies, and processed vocals. “The whole first record, we were just fucking around in the old Geese practice space,” Faber says. Both of them were listening to a lot of vaporwave at the time, and Faber was going through a Smashing Pumpkins phase that had piqued her interest in “this glitchy, grungy thing,” she says. “And I was less confident singing, too, so I was like, ‘I’m just going to Auto-Tune.'”.

“I was quite young,” adds Green, who turned 20 shortly after they met. “I hadn’t met anybody else who was transitioning until I met you. A lot of the songs were about that. According to recent reports, the next step was seeing what Star’s Revenge sounded like onstage. “You revealed me the songs, and I was like, ‘You’ve gotta play a show,'” says Billard, who knew Faber from their high school days on Long Island, as well as their overlapping stints in the band Turnip King in the 2010s. “In my heart, I was like, ‘Let me play.'”.

Rounded out by Ceballos on bass, the quartet lineup played their first show in August 2023 at a DIY space in Bushwick, followed by many more live dates around the city where they honed their approach and developed a more direct rock & roll sound. Faber and Green kept writing songs whenever they had time, and in 2024 — shortly after self-releasing the band’s debut — they began recording as a four-piece at Billard’s home studio in Port Washington, Upcoming York. “There was a bit of an interim period between 3D Country and Getting Killed,” Green notes, referencing Geese’s two most recent albums. “Cameron was working on his solo record. I had a lot of time at home, so there was time to work on this.”.

The making of Star’s Revenge II stretched out over more than two years. They ended up with a Bowiesque story about a fictional character named Star that also offers a richly rewarding glimpse of its creators’ interior lives.

Recent findings suggest that “Star is a girl that’s a star,” explains Faber, who has dreams of writing a series of books to build out the mythology. “She’s fallen from the sky down to earth and is trying to figure things out. She has to dissolve who she’s been, what she knows to be real, and relearn everything.”.

Faber indicates that the anthemic lead single, “Don’t Worry Dynamite,” is about “keeping your heart open, no matter how much it hurts, and keeping your heart as honest as you can.” Other songs, like the album opener “Clean,” reflect Faber’s personal journey toward sobriety. “It’s been six years of complete dissolving of any sense of reality,” she says, adding that she’s been sober since January 2026. “I finally feel like I’m on the other side of that…. I just feel like myself now.”.

Faber sings lead vocals on most of the album, which frees Green up to do what she most enjoys. “I love it when you come in with a fully-formed song and I get to just make a sick guitar part over it,” she tells Faber. “I don’t have to write the song. I can just shred. It’s fun.”.

In a recent development, in the past year especially, working with Star’s Revenge has given her a much-needed break from the hype cycle surrounding Geese. “A lot has happened with that band recently, and there’s a weight to all that,” Green says. “There’s this panopticon effect of it being a thing that people pay attention to. It’s heavy.” Playing with Star’s Revenge feels “pure” by contrast, she says — “similar to the way it felt to just play music in high school with friends.”.

When we meet for this interview, it’s only a few hours after the nominations are revealed for next year’s Grammys, with Geese up for five awards including Best New Artist. “What can I say? It’s an honor,” Green says. “It’s us and Angine de Poitrine, and we’re off to the races. I’d love to just battle it out in a ring.”.

“Like a battle of the bands,” Billard states.

“Yeah,” Green notes, laughing. “That’s how it should be fucking done, actually. That would be a truly democratic voting process.”.

As much fun as she’s having with Star’s Revenge, she’s also doing something she admits is hard: opening up. “This band has been a good lesson in vulnerability for me,” Green says. “There’s just less to hide behind, even on the base level of learning to have a relationship with my own voice. I didn’t really sing much before this. A lot of it is learning to do that, and to bare my heart to y’all — which I still have lots of difficulty with. But I’m trying.”.

It has been revealed that the album closes with “Something Missing,” a stunning psychedelic ballad that features Green’s lead vocals over softly looping guitars. “For the first time in my life, I’ve got the feeling I’m in love,” she sings. It came together at the very end of the recording sessions at Billard’s studio, taking up the final inches of tape they were working with.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 13:55 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 18 November 2026.

Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s new home or at least they will when everything is in order.

Tyler has recently moved house and the large, framed photograph of Teddy Sheringham scoring for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool, the only goal of the first Premier League game broadcast live by Sky is still on the floor by the front door.

From wherever it ends up, it will project a moment in time when everything changed for Tyler, having walked away from a steady job at ITV and taken a leap of faith as lead commentator for the new satellite channel.

'A new frontier,' admits Tyler, the undisputed ‘Voice of the Premier League’ by the time he left the role at Sky, more than 30 years later.

'We didn’t know where it would take us, so that was a special day. Feeling a bit like a pioneer. Wondering whether we were all on a fool’s errand. Some people turned down the job I accepted because of the risk. My kids were four and two at the time.

'We used to travel to the games by train in those days, and we would look out of the window and count the satellite dishes as we passed through a big town. We didn’t know whether it was going to work. I wasn’t sure anybody would be watching.

Legendary football commentator Martin Tyler has released a book: TALES FROM THE GANTRY.

Tyler was the undoubted 'Voice of the Premier League' by the time he left Sky Sports in 2023.

'It was slow off the ground and there was a feeling within the game against live football, that people wouldn’t go to the games if they were televised live, and it ended up the opposite. Attendances have gone up, an amazing paradox. Now you can’t get a ticket.'.

Televised football has come a long way since Tyler’s first commentary game, Southampton v Sheffield Wednesday in the old Division Two in 1974, shot with just four cameras for Southern Television.

'Now if you don’t have 24 cameras you can feel a bit short-changed,' he laughs. 'I worked at ITV for about 17 years, most of it commentating and you would get a crew on match day who had been doing Coronation Street or Emmerdale Farm in the week and a match director from light entertainment.'.

According to recent reports, the Premier League has come a long way, too. Some might argue too far. It has led football from its roots as the working man’s game to a place where clubs are owned by nations states and mired in the legal complications of the Manchester City case.

Tyler wants to reserve comment on City’s financial offences until sentencing is passed, aware he is inextricably bound to their success because of his iconic commentary for Sergio Aguero’s winner in the 93rd minute against Queen’s Park Rangers to snatch the Premier League title from Manchester United in 2012.

'I’ve always noted you won’t see anything like it again, and I stick to that,' he states, although he the 'Aguero moment’ as it has become commonly known probably means less to him than it does to others.

He is proud to deliver the words but insists those moments belong to the players, the clubs and the fans, not to him.

Ask about his favourite game from three decades in the Premier League and Tyler instinctively pulls Liverpool’s 4-3 comeback win against Newcastle in 1996 from the thrillers he has called.

His own footballing background, meanwhile, could hardly be any further from the Premier League’s glitzy, moneyed elite.

Tyler has always supported Woking and played as an amateur for Corinthian-Casuals. 'The law was you couldn’t get paid,' he notes. 'We were on expenses only and they weren’t dodgy expenses. If I went on the tube to Leytonstone, I got the tube fare repaid and no more.

According to recent reports, 'I played for five years at that level and never got a penny because that was the rule. I played my last game in 1973 and within two years’ they got rid of it because so many people were bending the rules. An opposition player told me their team were on £75 a game.'.

Tyler reflected on his time in the game as a player, coach and commentator with Daily Mail Sport's Matt Barlow.

He was famously on commentary for Sergio Aguero's title-winning moment in 2012.

From a cricketing family, Tyler was on the books at Surrey where he twice served as 12th man and lived for a time with Bob Willis, who became one of England’s greatest fast bowlers after moving on to Warwickshire.

Sources indicate that his manager for a time at Casuals was Surrey legend Micky Stewart, who had also played for the famous amateur football club before turning professional at Charlton. In those days it was possible for the multi-talented to hold down a decent career in two sports.

An afternoon in Tyler’s company is just as likely to involve digressions into non-league football, where he worked as an assistant to Alan Dowson at clubs including Woking and Hampton & Richmond, as it is into the Premier League.

He might regale you with a story about Arsene Wenger and the time, on the way to the gantry at Wigan Athletic, he slipped deeper than he realised into long conversation with the then Arsenal boss about rioting in Paris and almost missed his pre-match slot.

Recent findings suggest that and he might pivot from there into Wenger’s fierce rivalry with Sir Alex Ferguson. 'I have seen Arsene very, very grumpy,' indicates Tyler. 'When he lost the FA Cup semi-final when Dennis Bergkamp missed the penalty and Ryan Giggs scored.

It has been revealed that 'I have never seen a manager so angry because he knew he had handed over not only an FA Cup final place but also the domination they enjoyed at that time. They had done the Double in 98 and he felt that was not only about losing a match but losing their psychological edge over their greatest rivals. He was livid. Talk about winning and losing with dignity.'.

But there’s every chance he will reminisce about the time when, as a schoolboy Woking supporter in the terrible winter of 1962-63 he was rewarded for volunteering to paint the stands with an invitation to travel on the team bus to an Amateur Cup tie at Lydbrook Athletic.

Industry observers note that 'We left Woking at seven on the morning of the match for a two o’clock kick-off in Gloucestershire and by nine we were digging the bus out of a snowdrift on the A4,' indicates Tyler. 'We got there at four, no floodlights, and they had marked the lines on the snow with blue soap powder but there was no way we could play. We turned around to go back, got stuck in Cheltenham and had to stay for the night.'.

The only other footballing image on display in Tyler’s home is a photograph of him and Dowson celebrating as the final whistle confirmed their Hampton & Richmond side as Isthmian League champions in 2016.

Tyler has had a hugely varied career, all the way from grassroots level right to the top.

Tyler even worked as an assistant coach to Alan Dowson at several Non-League clubs.

TALES FROM THE GANTRY: Letters from a Lifetime in Football by Martin Tyler is published by Pitch and out now HERE.

After collecting the trophy, Tyler jumped into his car, drove north and less than 24 hours later was at the King Power Stadium to see Leicester crowned champions of England.

'The greatest fairytale story in the Premier League,' as he says. 'I had sampled that in a tiny non-league way, then taken those feelings with me to Leicester where it was multiplied a million times, but I could tell the world a tiny bit about how wonderful they must be feeling.'.

In a recent development, the range of his experience is vast. From amateur football in the 60s, through regional television and ITV to Sky’s Premier League revolution. He commentates regularly and coaches at Woking’s academy and has written a book.

In a recent development, it is a wonderful compilation of 110 essays, the reflections on his lifetime in football. 'The random thoughts of a football obsessive,' as he likes to call it.

TALES FROM THE GANTRY: Letters from a Lifetime in Football by Martin Tyler is published by Pitch and out now HERE.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

En direct de France, c’est samedi soir! Months after Saturday Night Live crossed the pond for a British production of the celebrated sketch show, its producers have eyes set on taking the Chunnel south. Variety reports that comedian and actor Manu Payet will host the inaugural episode of SNL France on Dec. 19. RnBoi, a French R&B artist, will be the first musical guest.

The show will mirror its U.S. and U.K. counterparts with a mix of live sketches, prerecorded segments, and musical guests all filmed before a studio audience. This one, however, will run only 52 minutes. Its inaugural cast will feature 10 actors.

According to recent reports, variety reports that SNL France’s producers spent a week shadowing their American counterparts to glean how the show operates. The writing team of Hugo Benamozig and David Caviglioli, who’ve scored hits in the country with Le Flambeau, Platane, and Terrible Jungle, will adapt the practices for a French audience. Just like the American version, the sketches will address French culture, entertainment, and politics, the last of which is notable as the country has a presidential election scheduled for 2027. Trending Stories Billy Ray Cyrus Shares Snapshots From Miley’s Wedding: ‘Beautiful’ to See Family ‘United by Love’ Anthem Singer Apologizes for ‘O Canada’ Flub at Leafs-Islanders Game U2 Will Bring Their ‘Greatest Show on Earth’ Stadium Tour to North America in 2027 Watch Taylor Swift Surprise Brenda Lee With ‘Rockin’ Around the Christmas Tree’ Honor.

The British version of SNL debuted in March and is now in its second season. Its success indicates broad appeal for the show, which has also been franchised out to South Korea where SNL Korea has won awards and even inspired a spinoff, The Smile Clinic, according to Variety. France previously attempted an SNL spinoff in 2017 but it lasted only one episode.

“With SNL France, our ambition is not to replicate a model, but to reinterpret its codes through a uniquely French lens,” Jean-Marc Juramie, deputy CEO of Canal+ France, which will air the show told Variety.

Apple fires back at Epic over claims it withheld 122,000 documents

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions.
  • While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

As part of the proceedings, Epic had submitted 16 categories of documents it wanted Apple to produce (including “internal analyses of the financial or business impact” of its proposed commissions and “communications relating to any strategies to dissuade developers from offering link-outs”), along with a list of current and former Apple employees whose records should be searched.

Apple agreed to use Epic’s proposed search terms and include all employees, and began producing documents it determined were responsive to Epic’s requests.

Epic, however, noted last Friday that Apple was improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching those search terms from the records of the seven initial employees, and asked the court to order Apple to produce all matching non-privileged documents, regardless of its relevance assessments.

Which brings us to Apple’s newest filing.

In its filing, Apple argues that contrary to Epic’s claim that its proposed search terms were “tailored” to the proceedings over link-out fees, they were actually “overbroad,” capturing large numbers of unrelated documents.

For instance, Apple notes that while intended to identify documents related to its proposed commission rates, Epic’s “commission*” search term also “captures documents that refer to government and private commissions, as well as documents hitting on the totally irrelevant term ‘commissioner,’ such as documents discussing the NFL Commissioner.”.

“[…] the use of a wildcard in a search string is designated by the asterisk symbol, which means that the search string will hit on any term that includes the prefix before the asterisk.

In the same vein, Apple notes that “Epic’s use of ‘fee*’ in its search strings related to litigation and Apple’s link-out-related projects pulled in documents containing words like ‘feel,’ ‘feed,’ ‘feedback,’ ‘feet,’ and ‘feeble’ without the word ‘fee’ or ‘fees’ appearing at all.”.

Apple’s overall argument is that these unrelated matches account for the vast majority of documents identified by Epic’s searches, and it cites legal precedent to argue that it should only be required to produce documents responsive to Epic’s requests, rather than every document matching the agreed-upon search terms:.

Sources indicate that in fact, at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms like these and did not include any reference to the term “link-out” or its variations, despite that concept being central to the Proffer and related discovery. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

Recent findings suggest that the law is clear: parties are only required to produce responsive documents, not every document returned by a search string. […] (“The Court will not compel defendants to produce any document simply because it contains a search term whether or not it is responsive to the discovery request.”). Epic has not shown, and cannot show, why the regular discovery process should be disrupted here. Speculation based on hit counts, particularly where the producing party can explain low responsiveness rates, does not justify the extraordinary and unprecedented remedy Epic seeks.

Apple goes on to argue that complying with Epic’s demands would require extensive additional work, including reviewing documents for privileged or sensitive information and redacting protected material, making it impossible to meet Epic’s proposed December 2 deadline.

Finally, Apple asks the court to reject Epic’s motion but proposes that, should the court decide that some intervention is warranted, a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deems nonresponsive be submitted to a Special Master for independent review, rather than producing all of them to Epic directly.

How Le Sserafim Unlocked a Newly introduced Kind of Fearlessness

💡 Key Takeaways
  • B efore Kim Chaewon could be fearless, she had to convince herself that she was.
  • When Le Sserafim debuted in 2022, the group’s name was a declaration, an anagram of “I’m Fearless.” Their debut single of the same name was equally assured, a cool, minimalist statement of ambition from a group of young women determined to make their mark on K-pop.
  • It has been revealed that but confidence isn’t easy to maintain, especially in an industry where every note, dance move, and perceived misstep can become fodder for public debate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

B efore Kim Chaewon could be fearless, she had to convince herself that she was.

When Le Sserafim debuted in 2022, the group’s name was a declaration, an anagram of “I’m Fearless.” Their debut single of the same name was equally assured, a cool, minimalist statement of ambition from a group of young women determined to make their mark on K-pop. Chaewon, the group’s leader, and Miyawaki Sakura were already seasoned idols, having performed together in the project group IZ*ONE. Huh Yunjin, a Korean American singer-songwriter raised in New York, brought her own artistic aspirations. Nakamura Kazuha had spent years training as a classical ballerina before making the leap into K-pop, while Hong Eunchae, the youngest, was just 15 when she debuted. Together, they were building an identity around a word that seemed to leave little room for uncertainty.

It has been revealed that but confidence isn’t easy to maintain, especially in an industry where every note, dance move, and perceived misstep can become fodder for public debate. For Chaewon, fearlessness was something she had to practice. Coming off IZ*ONE’s rapid success, she remembers being genuinely afraid in Le Sserafim’s early days, quietly encouraging herself to be brave, as though courage were something she could summon through sheer repetition.

“Personally, I think I was actually quite scared in our ‘fearless’ years,” Chaewon recalls, reflecting on those early days as she sits in the Rolling Stone studio in Fresh York. “So I used to repeat ‘fearless, fearless’ to myself, like I was casting a spell.”.

Chaewon can laugh about it now. The 26-year-old singer has spent much of her adult life onstage. She’s performed for tens of thousands of fans, traveled across continents, and weathered the kind of scrutiny that comes with growing up in the public eye. These days, she has a different relationship with fear. “That feeling of fearlessness used to be about guts and courage, but after all this time, my fearlessness comes from accepting some fear,” she explains. “When I’m a little scared, I tell myself something like, ‘Yeah, I’m scared. So what?'” There’s a certain freedom in that, in being able to set down some of the expectations she once carried and keep going. “By accepting that, I feel stronger,” she adds. In a recent development, sakura, at 28, has been an idol for more than half her life. She debuted in Japan, where she grew up, at just 13, long before Le Sserafim, and she has spent much of her adolescence and adulthood navigating the expectations that come with public life. Earlier in her career, she struggled to acknowledge her own fears. “I used to feel the most scared when I couldn’t accept the imperfections within myself,” she admits. But age and experience have changed the way she sees herself. “I’ve learned to accept that I still have room to grow, and that’s allowed me to love myself more,” she claims. That acceptance has given her a greater sense of freedom, making it easier to embrace new challenges head-on.

Recent findings suggest that it also helps that Sakura, or Saki, as she’s affectionately known, has weathered the storm of public opinion long enough to develop a healthy dose of perspective. She’s learned that not every opinion about her deserves her attention.

For Yunjin, fear has become something worth examining rather than escaping. “I feel like fear is such a multidimensional emotion,” the 25-year-old singer indicates thoughtfully. “You’re scared of something because you love it so much, or you’re scared of something because you want to hold on to it that much, and it’s that meaningful to you.” Over the years, she’s come to recognize that being afraid doesn’t necessarily mean you’re doing something wrong. Sometimes, it means you’re doing something that matters. “I’ve really learned over the few years that we’ve been together that true strength and true empowerment is to do things scared and do it anyway, even when you’re in the midst of fear,” she says.
